units.zh: 處前者為君長，在後者為臣僕。
units.en: The fore ranks play lord; the rear play slave.
units.literal: Those in front are lords and elders; those behind are servants and slaves.

units.zh: 君長者豐衍而有餘，臣僕者窮竭而不足。
units.en: Front ranks swim in surplus; the rear run dry.
units.literal: The lords overflow with plenty; the servants are drained and wanting.

units.zh: 《詩》云：「哿矣富人，哀此煢獨。」
units.en: As the Classic of Poetry says, 'Happy the rich—pity the poor alone.'
units.literal: The Odes says, 'How pleasant the rich man; pity these alone and helpless.'

units.zh: 錢之為言泉也，無遠不往，無幽不至。
units.en: Cash means 'springwater': it runs everywhere, even to the dark.
units.literal: As for cash, the word means 'spring': nothing far it does not go, nothing hidden it does not reach.

units.zh: 京邑衣冠，疲勞講肄，厭聞清談，對之睡寐，見我家兄，莫不驚視。
units.en: Luoyang's gentry, bored with seminars, nap through abstruse talk yet snap awake at Elder Brother.
units.literal: The caps and gowns of the capital, weary of lectures, tired of pure conversation, fall asleep facing it; when they see my elder brother none fail to stare wide-eyed.

units.zh: 錢之所祐，吉無不利，何必讀書，然後富貴！
units.en: Where it blesses, luck follows—who needs books if cash smiles?
units.literal: Where cash lends its aid, auspicious is nothing not favorable—why must one read books and only then become noble and rich!

units.zh: 昔呂公欣悅於空版，漢祖克之於贏二，文君解布裳而被錦繡，相如乘高蓋而解犢鼻，官尊名顯，皆錢所致。
units.en: Lü Gong bowed to an empty bond, Gaozu won with two extra coins, Zhuo Wenjun traded sackcloth for silk, Sima Xiangru swapped cowherd shorts for a grand carriage—every rise came from cash.
units.literal: In old days Lord Lü rejoiced in an empty tally, Han's founder conquered with an extra two cash; Wenjun cast off her linen skirt for brocade, Xiangru rode a high canopy and shed his calf-nose apron—rank high and names bright were all brought about by cash.

units.zh: 空版至虛，而況有實；
units.en: An empty bond is hollow—think what solid coin can do.
units.literal: The empty tally is utmost void—how much more what has substance!

units.zh: 贏二雖少，以致親密。
units.en: Two little coins bought an empire's favor.
units.literal: The extra two were few, yet they won intimacy.

units.zh: 由此論之，謂為神物。
units.en: So men call it divine.
units.literal: Judging by this, call it a numinous thing.

units.zh: 無德而尊，無勢而熱，排金門而入紫闥。
units.en: Virtueless yet revered, powerless yet mighty—it shoulders past the palace gates.
units.literal: Without virtue yet honored, without power yet hot—it pushes the golden gate and enters the purple portals.

units.zh: 危可使安，死可使活，貴可使賤，生可使殺。
units.en: It turns peril to peace, death to life, honor to shame, and living men to corpses.
units.literal: Danger it can make safe; death it can make live; noble it can make base; alive it can make killed.

units.zh: 是故忿爭非錢不勝，幽滯非錢不拔，怨仇非錢不解，令問非錢不發。
units.en: No feud ends, no deadlock lifts, no grudge clears, no fair name flies without its nod.
units.literal: Therefore in angry quarrel without cash you do not win; in hidden obstruction without cash you do not rise; in hatred and vengeance without cash you do not resolve; in fair fame without cash you does not spread.

units.zh: 洛中硃衣，當途之士，愛我家兄，皆我已已。
units.en: Crimson officials and palace climbers never tire of my elder brother Kongfang.
units.literal: The vermilion robes of Luoyang, the men who block the road—all love my elder brother and never weary of him.

units.zh: 執我之手，抱我終始，不計優劣，不論年紀，賓客輻輳，門常如市。
units.en: They shake his hand from youth to age, heedless of rank or years; his gate is always a market.
units.literal: They grasp my hand and cling to my end, reckoning neither better nor worse, speaking neither of age; guests crowd like spokes to a hub, the gate ever like a market.

units.zh: 諺曰：「錢無耳，可使鬼。」
units.en: The proverb runs, 'Money has no ears, but it can command ghosts.'
units.literal: The proverb says, 'Cash has no ears, yet can move ghosts.'

units.zh: 凡今之人，惟錢而已。
units.en: So men today worship only cash.
units.literal: As for people today, it is only cash.

units.zh: 故曰軍無財，士不來；
units.en: Hence the saying: no pay, no troops.
units.literal: Therefore it is said, an army without wealth, its knights will not come;

units.zh: 軍無賞，士不往。
units.en: No bounty, no charge.
units.literal: An army without rewards, its knights will not go.

units.zh: 仕無中人，不如歸田。
units.en: Serve without a broker in the ministry and you may as well plow.
units.literal: Without a go-between in office, better to return to the fields.

units.zh: 雖有中人，而無家兄，不異無翼而欲飛，無足而欲行。
units.en: Even with a patron, without Kongfang you are a bird without wings, a man without legs.
units.literal: Even if there is a go-between, without my elder brother it is no different from wishing to fly without wings or walk without feet.

units.zh: 蓋疾時者共傳其文。
units.en: Every cynic of the age copied his essay.
units.literal: In general those who hated the times together passed around his text.

units.zh: 褒不仕，莫知其所終。
units.en: Bao never served; no one knows his end.
units.literal: Bao did not take office; none knows where he ended.

units.zh: 氾騰，字無忌，敦煌人也。
units.en: Fan Teng, courtesy name Wuji, came from Dunhuang.
units.literal: Fan Teng, styled Wuji, was a man of Dunhuang.

units.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中。
units.en: Raised as filial-incorrupt, he became a gentleman of the palace.
units.literal: He was recommended filial and incorrupt and appointed gentleman of the palace.

units.zh: 屬天下兵亂，去官還家。
units.en: When war swept the empire he resigned and went home.
units.literal: When the realm fell into military chaos, he left office and returned home.

units.zh: 太守張閟造之，閉門不見，禮遺一無所受。
units.en: Prefect Zhang Min called; he barred the door and refused every gift.
units.literal: Prefect Zhang Min visited him; he shut the gate and would not see him, and accepted none of the courteous gifts.

units.zh: 歎曰：「生於亂世，貴而能貧，乃可以免。」
units.en: He said, 'In a dark age stay high-minded and poor—that is how you survive.'
units.literal: He sighed, saying, "Born in a disorderly age, to be noble yet able to be poor—only thus can one escape."

units.zh: 散家財五十萬，以施宗族，柴門灌園，琴書自適。
units.en: He gave away half a million to kin, wattled his gate, hoed his garden, and took his ease with lute and books.
units.literal: He scattered fifty myriad cash of family wealth to give to his lineage kin, wattled his gate, irrigated his garden, and with zither and books pleased himself.

units.zh: 張軌徵之為府司馬，騰曰：「門一杜，其可開乎！」
units.en: Zhang Gui wanted him as marshal; Teng said, "A shut gate should not reopen!"
units.literal: Zhang Gui summoned him as clerk to his headquarters; Teng said, "Once the gate is shut, can it be opened!"

units.zh: 固辭。
units.en: He refused flatly.
units.literal: He firmly declined.

units.zh: 病兩月餘而卒。
units.en: He died after two months' illness.
units.literal: After more than two months of illness he died.

units.zh: 任旭，字次龍，臨海章安人也。
units.en: Ren Xu, courtesy name Cilong, came from Zhang'an in Linhai.
units.literal: Ren Xu, styled Cilong, was a man of Zhang'an in Linhai.

units.zh: 父訪，吳南海太守。
units.en: His father Ren Fang had governed Nanhai under Wu.
units.literal: His father Fang was governor of Nanhai for Wu.

units.zh: 旭幼孤弱，兒童時勤於學。
units.en: Orphaned young, he studied with fierce diligence.
units.literal: Xu in youth was orphaned and weak; in childhood he was diligent in study.

units.zh: 及長，立操清修，不染流俗，鄉曲推而愛之。
units.en: Grown, he kept his life clean and won the hamlet's love.
units.literal: When grown, he established conduct clear and cultivated, dyed not by vulgar currents; the village pushed him forward and loved him.

units.zh: 郡將蔣秀嘉其名，請為功曹。
units.en: General Jiang Xiu of the commandery, admiring him, asked him to serve as merit clerk.
units.literal: The commandery general Jiang Xiu admired his name and invited him to be merit clerk.

units.zh: 秀居官貪穢，每不奉法，旭正色苦諫。
units.en: Jiang Xiu was corrupt and lawless; Xu rebuked him bluntly again and again.
units.literal: Xiu in office was greedy and foul, often not obeying the law; Xu with stern countenance bitterly remonstrated.

units.zh: 秀既不納，旭謝去，閉門講習，養志而已。
units.en: When Xiu brushed him off, Xu resigned, barred his door, and lived for his studies and his conscience.
units.literal: Xiu would not accept; Xu took leave, shut his gate, lectured and studied, and nourished his intent only.

units.zh: 久之，秀坐事被收，旭狼狽營送，秀慨然歎曰：「任功曹真人也。
units.en: When Xiu fell under arrest, Xu scrambled to help him on his way; Xiu sighed, 'Ren Xu is the real thing.
units.literal: After a long while Xiu was seized on a charge; Xu in disarray worked to send him off; Xiu sighed with feeling, saying, "Clerk Ren is a true man.

units.zh: 吾違其讜言，以至於此，復何言哉！」
units.en: I ignored his straight talk and came to this—what is left to say?'
units.literal: I disobeyed his blunt counsel and reached this pass—what more is there to say!"

units.zh: 尋察孝廉，除郎中，州郡仍舉為郡中正，固辭歸家。
units.en: Soon Xu passed as filial-incorrupt, served briefly as gentleman, was pressed to be local evaluator, and each time went home instead.
units.literal: Soon he was examined filial and incorrupt, appointed gentleman of the palace; the province and commandery again nominated him as impartial and just for the commandery; he firmly declined and returned home.

units.zh: 永康初，惠帝博求清節俊異之士，太守仇馥薦旭清貞潔素，學識通博，詔下州郡以禮發遣。
units.en: In Yongkang 1 Emperor Hui cast a wide net for recluses; Prefect Qiu Fu praised Xu's purity and learning, and the court ordered him escorted with honors.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yongkang, Emperor Hui broadly sought men of pure integrity and outstanding talent; Prefect Qiu Fu recommended Xu as chaste, clean, plain, his learning broad and penetrating; an edict ordered the commandery to dispatch him with ritual.

units.zh: 旭以朝廷多故，志尚隱遁，辭疾不行。
units.en: Xu pleaded illness—the court was chaos and his heart was in the hills.
units.literal: Xu, because the court had many troubles, his aspiration inclined to hidden retreat, pleaded illness and did not go.

units.zh: 尋天下大亂，陳敏作逆，江東名豪並見羈縶，惟旭與賀循守死不回。
units.en: When Chen Min rose, every Jiangdong notable was caged; only Xu and He Xun chose death over submission.
units.literal: Soon the realm fell into great chaos; Chen Min rebelled; the famous magnates east of the Yang were all seized and bound; only Xu and He Xun guarded death and would not turn.

units.zh: 敏卒不能屈。
units.en: Chen Min never broke them.
units.literal: Min in the end could not bend them.

units.zh: 元帝初鎮江東，聞其名，召為參軍，手書與旭，欲使必到，旭固辭以疾。
units.en: Emperor Yuan, first settling the east, summoned him as staff adviser and wrote in his own hand; Xu still pleaded sickness.
units.literal: When Emperor Yuan first garrisoned the east, hearing his name he summoned him as adviser, personally wrote to Xu wishing to make him surely come; Xu firmly declined on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 後帝進位鎮東大將軍，復召之；
units.en: When the prince rose to general of the east, he called again;
units.literal: Later when the emperor advanced to general who stabilizes the east, he summoned him again;

units.zh: 及為左丞相，辟為祭酒，並不就。
units.en: when he became left chancellor he offered the wine-cup post—Xu refused every one.
units.literal: and when he became left chancellor, he summoned him as libationer—he took none of these posts.

units.zh: 中興建，公車徵，會遭母憂。
units.en: At the court's revival the summons came; his mother died that same hour.
units.literal: When the restoration was founded, the state carriage summoned him; it happened he encountered mourning for his mother.

units.zh: 于時司空王導啟立學校，選天下明經之士，旭與會稽虞喜俱以隱學被召。
units.en: Wang Dao then opened schools and wanted Xu and Yu Xi, famed recluses, to join.
units.literal: At that time Minister Wang Dao proposed establishing schools and selecting men of clear classics from the empire; Xu with Yu Xi of Kuaiji were both summoned for their hidden learning.

units.zh: 事未行，會有王敦之難，尋而帝崩，事遂寢。
units.en: Wang Dun's coup came first; the emperor died; the plan died with him.
units.literal: The affair had not been carried out when there occurred Wang Dun's rebellion; soon the emperor died, and the matter then lapsed.

units.zh: 明帝即位，又徵拜給事中，旭稱疾篤，經年不到，尚書以稽留除名，僕射荀崧議以為不可。
units.en: Emperor Ming named him palace counselor; Xu stayed away a year until the ministry struck his name—Xun Song protested.
units.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, he again summoned and appointed him palace counselor; Xu claimed grave illness, and for a full year did not arrive; the ministry struck his name for delay, but vice-director Xun Song argued it should not be done.

units.zh: 太寧末，明帝復下詔備禮徵旭，始下而帝崩。
units.en: Late in Taining another honored summons went out; the edict landed the day the emperor died.
units.literal: At the end of Taining, Emperor Ming again issued an edict summoning Xu with full ritual; the edict had just been issued when the emperor died.

units.zh: 咸和二年卒，太守馮懷上疏謂宜贈九列值蘇峻作亂，事竟不行。
units.en: He died in Xianhe 2; Feng Huai asked posthumous rank to the Nine Ministers, but Su Jun's revolt buried the request.
units.literal: He died in the second year of Xianhe; Prefect Feng Huai submitted a memorial saying he should be posthumously honored to the nine ranks, but it happened Su Jun rebelled, and the affair in the end was not carried out.

units.zh: 子琚，位至大宗正，終於家。
units.en: His son Ren Ju reached grand director of the imperial surname and died at home.
units.literal: His son Ju rose to grand director of the imperial clan and ended his life at home.

units.zh: 郭文，字文舉，河內軹人也。
units.en: Guo Wen, courtesy name Wenju, came from Zhi in Henei.
units.literal: Guo Wen, styled Wenju, was a man of Zhi in Henei.

units.zh: 少愛山水，尚嘉遁。
units.en: He loved wild country and the name of recluse.
units.literal: In youth he loved mountains and rivers and esteemed fine reclusion.

units.zh: 年三十，每游山林，彌旬忘反。
units.en: At thirty he would vanish into the hills for weeks on end.
units.literal: At thirty he often roamed forests and mountains, forgetting to return for a full ten days.

units.zh: 父母終，服畢，不娶，辭家遊名山，歷華陰之崖，以觀石室之石函。
units.en: After burying his parents he took no wife, left kin, and climbed Huayin to see the stone reliquary.
units.literal: When his parents died and mourning was finished, he did not marry, left home to roam famous mountains, passed the cliffs of Huayin to view the stone casket in the stone chamber.

units.zh: 洛陽陷，乃步擔入吳興余杭大辟山中窮谷無人之地，倚木於樹，苫覆其上而居焉，亦無壁障。
units.en: When Luoyang fell he walked into the Pi range in Yuhang, leaned poles against trees, thatched a roof, and lived without walls.
units.literal: When Luoyang fell, he shouldered a carrying-pole and walked into the great Pi mountains of Wuxing Yuhang, to a remote valley without men; he leaned timbers on trees, thatched above them, and dwelt there, without even a wall.

units.zh: 時猛獸為暴，入屋害人，而文獨宿十餘年，卒無患害。
units.en: Beasts raided every hut but left him alone for ten years.
units.literal: At the time fierce beasts ravaged, entering houses and harming people, yet Wen alone lodged there more than ten years and in the end suffered no harm.

units.zh: 恆著鹿裘葛巾，不飲酒食肉，區種菽麥，采竹葉木實，貿鹽以自供。
units.en: He wore buckskin and hemp kerchief, ate no meat, hoed beans, lived on forage, and traded for salt.
units.literal: He constantly wore deerskin and a ge cloth kerchief, drank no wine and ate no meat, hoed beans and wheat, gathered bamboo leaves and tree fruits, and bartered for salt to supply himself.

units.zh: 人或酬下價者，亦即與之。
units.en: If buyers underpaid, he let them.
units.literal: If someone paid a low price, he still gave it to him.

units.zh: 後人識文，不復賤酬。
units.en: Once they knew him, they paid fair coin.
units.literal: Later when people recognized Wen, they no longer underpaid.

units.zh: 食有餘穀，輒恤窮匱。
units.en: He shared spare grain with the hungry.
units.literal: When he had surplus grain he always relieved the destitute.

units.zh: 人有臻遺，取其粗者，示不逆而已。
units.en: When gifts came he took only the plain pieces to show courtesy, not greed.
units.literal: When people brought gifts he took only the coarse items, showing he did not refuse outright.

units.zh: 有猛獸殺大麀鹿於庵側，文以語人，人取賣之，分錢與文。
units.en: A wild beast killed a large deer beside his hut; he told neighbors, they sold it and offered him coin.
units.literal: A fierce beast killed a large deer beside his hut; Wen told people; they took and sold it and divided the cash with Wen.

units.zh: 文曰：「我若須此，自當賣之。
units.en: Wen said, 'Had I wanted money I would have sold it myself.
units.literal: Wen said, "If I needed this, I would have sold it myself.

units.zh: 所以相語，正以不須故也。」
units.en: I mentioned it only because I do not need the money.'
units.literal: The reason I told you was precisely because I do not need it."

units.zh: 聞者皆嗟歎之。
units.en: Hearing this, they marveled.
units.literal: Those who heard all sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 嘗有猛獸忽張口向文，文視其口中有橫骨，乃以手探去之，猛獸明旦致一鹿於其室前。
units.en: A beast gaped at him; he pulled a bone from its jaw; at dawn it laid a deer before his door.
units.literal: Once a fierce beast suddenly opened its mouth toward Wen; Wen saw a crossbone stuck in its mouth, then reached with his hand and removed it; the next morning the fierce beast brought a deer before his chamber.

units.zh: 獵者時往寄宿，文夜為擔水而無倦色。
units.en: Hunters camped with him; he fetched their water night after night, untiring.
units.literal: Hunters sometimes came to lodge overnight; Wen by night carried water for them without a weary look.

units.zh: 余杭令顧颺與葛洪共造之，而攜與俱歸。
units.en: Magistrate Gu Yang and Ge Hong visited him and carried him back to town.
units.literal: The magistrate of Yuhang, Gu Yang, with Ge Hong together visited him and carried him back with them.

units.zh: 颺以文山行或須皮衣，贈以韋袴褶一具，文不納，辭歸山中。
units.en: Gu Yang gave him leather breeches for the cold; Wen refused and walked back to the hills.
units.literal: Yang, because Wen in mountain travel might need fur garments, presented him with one set of leather trousers and pleated jacket; Wen would not accept and returned to the mountains.

units.zh: 颺追遣使者置衣室中而去，文亦無言，韋衣乃至爛於戶內，竟不服用。
units.en: Yang left the clothes in his hut; Wen never touched them until they rotted on the floor.
units.literal: Yang afterward sent a messenger who placed the clothes in the chamber and departed; Wen also said nothing; the leather garments even rotted inside the door; in the end he never wore them.

units.zh: 王導聞其名，遣人迎之，文不肯就船車，荷擔徒行。
units.en: Wang Dao sent a coach; Wen shouldered his pole and walked.
units.literal: Wang Dao heard his name and sent men to welcome him; Wen would not board boat or cart, but shouldered a pole and went on foot.

units.zh: 既至，導置之西園，園中果木成林，又有鳥獸麋鹿，因以居文焉。
units.en: Wang Dao housed him in West Park among orchards and tame deer.
units.literal: When he arrived, Dao placed him in the West Park, where fruit trees made a forest and moreover there were birds, beasts, and deer—thereby he lodged Wen there.

units.zh: 於是朝士咸共觀之，文頹然踑踞，傍若無人。
units.en: Officials came to gawk; Wen squatted like a stone, indifferent to the crowd.
units.literal: Thereupon court gentlemen all together viewed him; Wen sat slumped, squatting with knees spread, as if no one were beside him.

units.zh: 溫嶠嘗問文曰：「人皆有六親相娛，先生棄之何樂？」
units.en: Wen Qiao asked Wen, "All men have six kin to enjoy themselves with—why do you abandon them, sir, and what joy is there?"
units.literal: Wen Qiao once asked Wen, "All men have six kin to enjoy themselves with—why do you abandon them, sir, and what joy is there?"

units.zh: 文曰：「本行學道，不謂遭世亂，欲歸無路，是以來也。」
units.en: Wen answered, 'I went out to study the Way; chaos penned me in with no road home—so I drifted here.'
units.literal: Wen said, "Originally I practiced the Way; I did not expect to meet the age in chaos; I wished to return but had no road—therefore I have come."

units.zh: 又問曰：「饑而思食，壯而思室，自然之性，先生安獨無情乎？」
units.en: Qiao pressed, "Hungry then one thinks of food; in vigor one thinks of chamber—such is nature's temper; how is it, sir, that you alone are without feeling?"
units.literal: Again he asked, "Hungry then one thinks of food; in vigor one thinks of chamber—such is nature's temper; how is it, sir, that you alone are without feeling?"

units.zh: 文曰：「情由憶生，不憶故無情。」
units.en: Wen said, 'Passion feeds on memory; I forget, so I am still.'
units.literal: Wen said, "Feeling arises from memory; without memory therefore there is no feeling."

units.zh: 又問曰：「先生獨處窮山，若疾病遭命，則為烏鳥所食，顧不酷乎？」
units.en: Qiao asked, "Sir, alone in a poor mountain, if illness meets fate, then you will be food for crows and kites—is it not cruel?"
units.literal: Again he asked, "Sir, alone in a poor mountain, if illness meets fate, then you will be food for crows and kites—is it not cruel?"

units.zh: 文曰：「藏埋者亦為螻蟻所食，復何異乎！」
units.en: Wen said, 'Buried men feed ants too—what is the difference?'
units.literal: Wen said, "Those who are buried in earth are also eaten by ants—is there any difference!"

units.zh: 又問曰：「猛獸害人，人之所畏，而先生獨不畏邪？」
units.en: Qiao asked, "Fierce beasts harm people; that is what men fear—yet sir, you alone are not afraid?"
units.literal: Again he asked, "Fierce beasts harm people; that is what men fear—yet sir, you alone are not afraid?"

units.zh: 文曰：「人無害獸之心，則獸亦不害人。」
units.en: Wen said, 'Men who wish beasts no harm need not fear them.'
units.literal: Wen said, "When men have no mind to harm beasts, then beasts also do not harm people."

units.zh: 又問曰：「苟世不寧，身不得安。
units.en: Qiao asked, "Suppose the age is not peaceful and the person cannot be secure.
units.literal: Again he asked, "Suppose the age is not peaceful and the person cannot be secure.

units.zh: 今將用先生以濟時，若何？」
units.en: Now we wish to employ sir to aid the times—how about it?"
units.literal: Now we wish to employ sir to aid the times—how about it?"

units.zh: 文曰：「山草之人，安能佐世！」
units.en: Wen laughed: 'A weed from the hills cannot prop the age.'
units.literal: Wen said, "A man of mountain grass—how can he assist the age!"

units.zh: 導嘗眾客共集，絲竹並奏，試使呼之。
units.en: Wang Dao once held a banquet with music and called him in.
units.literal: Dao once gathered many guests together; strings and winds played together; he tried ordering Wen summoned.

units.zh: 文瞪眸不轉，跨躡華堂如行林野。
units.en: Wen stared straight ahead and crossed the marble hall like a path in the woods.
units.literal: Wen stared without turning his eyes, strode across the splendid hall as though walking forest and field.

units.zh: 于時坐者咸有鉤深味遠之言，文常稱不達來語。
units.en: Guests spouted abstruse philosophy; Wen always said he could not follow.
units.literal: At that time those seated all had words that hooked the deep and tasted the far; Wen always said he did not understand the speech that had come.

units.zh: 天機鏗宏，莫有窺其門者。
units.en: His mind was a locked drum—no one found the key.
units.literal: Heaven's mechanism was vast and ringing; none could spy his gate.

units.zh: 溫嶠嘗稱曰：「文有賢人之性，而無賢人之才，柳下、梁踦之亞乎！」
units.en: Wen Qiao praised him, saying, "Wen has the nature of a worthy man but not the talent of a worthy man—perhaps he is of the class of Liuxia Hui and Liang Qi!"
units.literal: Wen Qiao once praised him, saying, "Wen has the nature of a worthy man but not the talent of a worthy man—perhaps he is of the class of Liuxia Hui and Liang Qi!"

units.zh: 永昌中，大疫，文病亦殆。
units.en: In Yongchang a plague swept the city; Wen nearly died.
units.literal: In the Yongchang period there was a great pestilence; Wen's illness also was near death.

units.zh: 王導遺藥，文曰：「命在天，不在藥也。
units.en: Wang Dao sent physic; Wen said, 'Life belongs to heaven, not to drugs.
units.literal: Wang Dao sent medicine; Wen said, "Life lies with heaven, not with medicine.

units.zh: 夭壽長短，時也。」
units.en: Long or short span is timing alone.'
units.literal: Short life or long is a matter of season."

units.zh: 居導園七年，未嘗出入。
units.en: Seven years in Wang Dao's park—never a step outside.
units.literal: He dwelt in Dao's park seven years and never went out.

units.zh: 一旦忽求還山，導不聽。
units.en: One dawn he begged to return; Wang Dao refused.
units.literal: One morning he suddenly begged to return to the mountains; Dao would not listen.

units.zh: 後逃歸臨安，結廬舍於山中。
units.en: He slipped back to Lin'an and raised a hut.
units.literal: Later he fled back to Lin'an and built a hut in the mountains.

units.zh: 臨安令萬寵迎置縣中。
units.en: Magistrate Wan Chong housed him in the yamen.
units.literal: The magistrate of Lin'an, Wan Chong, welcomed him and lodged him in the county.

units.zh: 及蘇峻反，破余杭，而臨安獨全，人皆異之，以為知機。
units.en: When Su Jun sacked Yuhang, Lin'an stood untouched—folk called it foresight.
units.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, he destroyed Yuhang, yet Lin'an alone remained intact; people all marveled, thinking he knew the pivot.

units.zh: 自後不復語，但舉手指麾，以宣其意。
units.en: After that he spoke only with hand signs.
units.literal: Afterward he no longer spoke but only raised his fingers in gesture to declare his intent.

units.zh: 病甚，求還山，欲枕石安屍，不令人殯葬，寵不聽。
units.en: Dying, he asked to lie on stone without funeral; Wan Chong refused.
units.literal: When his illness was severe he begged to return to the mountains, wishing to pillow his corpse on stone and not let men bury him; Chong would not listen.

units.zh: 不食二十餘日，亦不瘦。
units.en: He fasted twenty days yet never wasted.
units.literal: For more than twenty days he did not eat, yet he did not grow thin.

units.zh: 寵問曰：「先生復可得幾日？」
units.en: Wan Chong asked, "Sir, how many days have you left?"
units.literal: Chong asked, "Sir, how many days have you left?"

units.zh: 文三舉手，果以十五日終。
units.en: Wen raised his hand three times—he died on the fifteenth day as he signaled.
units.literal: Wen thrice raised his hand; indeed on the fifteenth day he died.

units.zh: 寵葬之于所居之處而祭哭之，葛洪、庾闡並為作傳，讚頌其美云。
units.en: Wan Chong buried him where he lived; Ge Hong and Yu Chan wrote his lives, praising his grace.
units.literal: Chong buried him at the place where he had dwelt and sacrificed and wept for him; Ge Hong and Yu Chan both composed biographies, praising and singing his excellence.

units.zh: 龔壯，字子瑋，巴西人也。
units.en: Gong Zhuang, courtesy name Ziwei, came from Baxi.
units.literal: Gong Zhuang, styled Ziwei, was a man of Baxi.

units.zh: 潔己自守，與鄉人譙秀齊名。
units.en: He matched his townsman Qiao Xiu for stainless repute.
units.literal: He kept himself pure and guarded his integrity, of one fame with his townsman Qiao Xiu.

units.zh: 父叔為李特所害，壯積年不除喪，力弱不能復仇。
units.en: Li Te had his father and uncle killed; Zhuang wore mourning for years, too weak to strike back.
units.literal: His father and uncle were killed by Li Te; Zhuang for years did not remove mourning, his strength being weak and unable to avenge.

units.zh: 及李壽戍漢中，與李期有嫌，期，特孫也，壯欲假壽以報，乃說壽曰：「節下若能並有西土，稱籓于晉，人必樂從。
units.en: When Li Shou feuded with Li Qi, Zhuang urged Shou, saying, "If you, sir, can swallow the western lands whole and declare vassalage to Jin, men will surely gladly follow.
units.literal: When Li Shou garrisoned Hanzhong and had a rift with Li Qi—Qi was Li Te's grandson—Zhuang wished to borrow Shou to take revenge, and therefore persuaded Shou, saying, "If you, sir, can swallow the western lands whole and declare vassalage to Jin, men will surely gladly follow.

units.zh: 且舍小就大，以危易安，莫大之策也。」
units.en: Trade a small throne for a great protectorship—no wiser plan.'
units.literal: Moreover to forsake the small and embrace the great, to trade peril for safety—there is no greater strategy."

units.zh: 壽然之，遂率眾討期，果克之。
units.en: Shou agreed, crushed Li Qi, and took power.
units.literal: Shou agreed, then led hosts to attack Qi and indeed overcame him.

units.zh: 壽猶襲偽號，欲官之，壯誓不仕，賂遺一無所取。
units.en: Shou still played emperor and offered posts; Zhuang refused every bribe.
units.literal: Shou still assumed a false title and wished to office him; Zhuang swore he would not serve and accepted none of the bribes or gifts.

units.zh: 會天久雨，百姓饑墊，壯上書說壽以歸順，允天心，應人望，永為國籓，福流子孫。
units.en: When famine came he memorialized Shou to yield to Jin and save the people.
units.literal: It happened heaven rained long; the people starved; Zhuang submitted a memorial urging Shou to submit, accord with heaven's mind, answer men's hopes, forever be a vassal state of the dynasty, and extend blessing to sons and grandsons.

units.zh: 壽省書內愧，秘而不宣。
units.en: Shou hid the memorial, ashamed.
units.literal: Shou read the letter, felt shame within, and hid it without proclaiming it.

units.zh: 乃遣使入胡，壯又諫之，壽又不納。
units.en: Shou then courted the Hu; Zhuang warned again; Shou ignored him.
units.literal: Then he sent envoys into the Hu; Zhuang again remonstrated; Shou again did not accept.

units.zh: 壯謂百行之本莫大忠孝，即假壽殺期，私仇以雪，又欲使其歸朝，以明臣節。
units.en: Zhuang had used Shou to kill his foe yet still wanted Jin's suzerainty honored.
units.literal: Zhuang considered that of the hundred conducts none is greater than loyalty and filial piety: having borrowed Shou to kill Qi, his private revenge was avenged, yet he also wished to make him return to court to clarify ministerial integrity.

units.zh: 壽既不從，壯遂稱聾，又云手不制物，終身不復至成都，惟研考經典，譚思文章，至李勢時卒。
units.en: When Shou refused, Zhuang feigned deafness and paralysis, never returned to Chengdu, studied until Li Shi's day, and died.
units.literal: Shou would not follow; Zhuang then claimed deafness, also said his hands could not grasp things, to the end of his life did not again go to Chengdu, only grinding through the classics and pondering texts, and died under Li Shi.

units.zh: 初，壯每歎中夏多經學，而巴蜀鄙陋，兼遭李氏之難，無復學徒，乃著《邁德論》，文多不載。
units.en: He wrote 'On Surpassing Virtue' to mourn learning lost in Shu—text omitted here.
units.literal: At first Zhuang often sighed that the central plain abounded in classical learning while Ba and Shu were rustic; moreover they suffered the Li clan's disasters and had no more students; therefore he composed the "On Surpassing Virtue"; the text is mostly not recorded here.

units.zh: 孟陋，字少孤，武昌人也。
units.en: Meng Lou, courtesy name Shaogu, came from Wuchang.
units.literal: Meng Lou, styled Shaogu, was a man of Wuchang.

units.zh: 吳司空宗之曾孫也。
units.en: He was great-grandson of Wu minister Meng Zong.
units.literal: He was great-grandson of Wu's minister of works Meng Zong.

units.zh: 兄嘉，桓溫征西長史。
units.en: His brother Meng Jia had been chief clerk under Huan Wen.
units.literal: His elder brother Meng Jia was chief clerk on Huan Wen's western campaign.

units.zh: 陋少而貞立，清操絕倫，布衣蔬食，以文籍自娛。
units.en: Young, he was chaste, austere, in sackcloth and gruel, happy only in books.
units.literal: Lou in youth was chaste and established, his pure conduct unmatched, in plain cloth and coarse food, taking pleasure in books.

units.zh: 口不及世事，未曾交遊，時或弋釣，孤興獨往，雖家人亦不知其所之也。
units.en: He never gossiped, rarely visited anyone, fished or hunted alone—his family never knew his path.
units.literal: His mouth did not touch the affairs of the age; he never socialized; sometimes he shot or fished, alone with his whim—even his household did not know where he went.

units.zh: 喪母，毀瘠殆於滅性，不飲酒食肉十有餘年。
units.en: His mother's death left him skeletal; he ate no meat over ten years.
units.literal: When his mother died, he wasted his flesh almost to extinguishing nature; for more than ten years he drank no wine and ate no meat.

units.zh: 親族迭謂之曰：「少孤！
units.en: Kinsmen pleaded, "Shaogu!
units.literal: Lineage kin in turn said to him, "Shaogu!

units.zh: 誰無父母？
units.en: Who has no parents?
units.literal: Who lacks parents?

units.zh: 誰有父母！
units.en: Who keeps parents forever?
units.literal: Who has parents!

units.zh: 聖人制禮，令賢者俯就，不肖企及。
units.en: The sages set rites so the wise may ease grief and fools may aim higher.
units.literal: The sages fixed ritual to let the worthy bend down and the unworthy strive up.

units.zh: 若使毀性無嗣，更為不孝也。」
units.en: To die childless is the greater unfilial act."
units.literal: If you destroy your nature and leave no heir, that is again unfilial.

units.zh: 陋感此言，然後從吉。
units.en: He heard them, relented, and ended mourning properly.
units.literal: Lou was moved by these words; then afterward he followed auspicious rites.

units.zh: 由是名著海內。
units.en: His name then filled the empire.
units.literal: From this his name was famed within the seas.

units.zh: 簡文帝輔政，命為參軍，稱疾不起。
units.en: Emperor Jianwen summoned him as adviser; he pleaded illness.
units.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he ordered him as adviser; he claimed illness and did not rise.

units.zh: 桓溫躬往造焉。
units.en: Huan Wen himself knocked on his door.
units.literal: Huan Wen in person went to visit him.

units.zh: 或謂溫曰：「孟陋高行，學為儒宗，宜引在府，以和鼎味。」
units.en: A friend told Huan Wen, 'Meng Lou's virtue tops the scholars; bring him to your staff to leaven the court.'
units.literal: Someone said to Wen, "Meng Lou's conduct is lofty; his learning is patriarch of Confucians—it is fitting to draw him into the office to harmonize the cauldron's flavor."

units.zh: 溫歎曰：「會稽王尚不能屈，非敢擬議也。」
units.en: Wen sighed, 'Even the prince of Kuaiji could not move him—I hardly dare speak of hiring him.'
units.literal: Wen sighed, saying, "The prince of Kuaiji still could not bend him—how dare I presume to discuss it."

units.zh: 陋聞之曰：「桓公正當以我不往故耳。
units.en: Lou heard and said, 'Huan Wen only thinks I snubbed him on purpose.
units.literal: Lou heard it and said, "Lord Huan only thinks it is because I did not go.

units.zh: 億兆之人，無官者十居其九，豈皆高士哉！
units.en: Nine men in ten lack office—are they all recluses?
units.literal: Of the myriad million men, nine in ten have no office—are they all lofty gentlemen!

units.zh: 我疾病不堪恭相王之命，非敢為高也。」
units.en: I am too sick to obey the prince's summons—that is no pose of pride.'
units.literal: I am ill and cannot bear the respectful commands of the minister king—it is not that I dare be lofty."

units.zh: 由是名稱益重。
units.en: His name only grew weightier after that.
units.literal: From this his reputation and title grew heavier.

units.zh: 博學多通，長於《三禮》。
units.en: He mastered the Three Rites.
units.literal: He was broadly learned and penetrating, excelling in the Three Rites.

units.zh: 注《論語》，行於世。
units.en: His Analects commentary circulates still.
units.literal: He annotated the Analects, which circulated in the world.

units.zh: 卒以壽終。
units.en: He died in ripe old age.
units.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.

units.zh: 韓績，字興齊，廣陵人也。
units.en: Han Ji, courtesy name Xingqi, came from Guangling.
units.literal: Han Ji, styled Xingqi, was a man of Guangling.

units.zh: 其先避亂，居於吳之嘉興。
units.en: His clan fled war and settled in Jiaxing.
units.literal: His ancestors fled turmoil and dwelt in Jiaxing of Wu.

units.zh: 父建，仕吳至大鴻臚。
units.en: His father Han Jian rose to grand herald under Wu.
units.literal: His father Jian served Wu to grand herald.

units.zh: 績少好文學，以潛退為操，布衣蔬食，不交當世，由是東土並宗敬焉。
units.en: He loved books, lived poor, shunned office, and the whole east coast revered him.
units.literal: Ji in youth loved letters and learning, taking hidden retirement as his conduct, in plain cloth and coarse food, not associating with the age—thereby the eastern lands together honored him.

units.zh: 司徒王導聞其名，辟以為掾，不就。
units.en: Wang Dao summoned him as clerk; he stayed away.
units.literal: Minister Wang Dao heard his name and summoned him as aide; he did not go.

units.zh: 咸康末，會稽內史孔愉上疏薦之，詔以安車束帛徵之。
units.en: Late in Xiankang Kong Yu recommended him; the court sent carriage and silk.
units.literal: At the end of Xiankang, interior secretary of Kuaiji Kong Yu submitted a memorial recommending him; an edict ordered him summoned with peace carriage and bundled silks.

units.zh: 尚書令諸葛恢奏績名望猶輕，未宜備禮，於是召拜博士。
units.en: Zhuge Hui said his name was still slight; the court named him erudite instead.
units.literal: Director of the secretariat Zhuge Hui memorialized that Ji's fame was still light and it was not yet fitting to use full ritual; thereupon he was summoned and appointed erudite.

units.zh: 稱老病不起，卒於家。
units.en: He pleaded age and died at home.
units.literal: He claimed old age and illness and would not rise; he died at home.

units.zh: 于時高密劉鮞字長魚、城陽邴郁字弘文，並有高名。
units.en: Liu Jun of Gaomi and Bing Yu of Chengyang shared his fame.
units.literal: At that time Liu Jun of Gaomi, styled Changyu, and Bing Yu of Chengyang, styled Hongwen, both had lofty names.

units.zh: 鮞幼不慕俗，長而希古，篤學厲行，化流邦邑。
units.en: Liu Jun scorned fashion, copied the ancients, and reshaped his town.
units.literal: Jun from youth did not admire the vulgar; grown, he aspired to antiquity, studied deeply and disciplined conduct, transforming his district.

units.zh: 郁，魏徵士原之曾孫，少有原風，敕身謹潔，口不妄說，耳不妄聽，端拱恂恂，舉動有禮。
units.en: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's great-grandson: silent, careful, every gesture correct.
units.literal: Yu was great-grandson of Wei recluse Bing Yuan; in youth he had Yuan's air, ordering the self chaste and clean, mouth not speaking rashly, ears not listening rashly, sitting upright and earnest, every motion with ritual.

units.zh: 咸康中，成帝博求異行之士，鮞、鬱並被公卿薦舉，於是依績及翟湯等例，以博士徵之。
units.en: Emperor Cheng sought odd talents; both were nominated like Han Ji and Zhai Tang.
units.literal: In Xiankang, Emperor Cheng broadly sought men of unusual conduct; Jun and Yu were together recommended by dukes and ministers; thereupon according to the precedent of Ji and Zhai Tang and others they were summoned as erudites.

units.zh: 鬱辭以疾，鮞隨使者到京師，自陳年老，不拜。
units.en: Yu pleaded sick; Liu Jun went to the capital, declared himself too old, and refused the cap.
units.literal: Yu declined on grounds of illness; Jun followed the envoy to the capital, personally declaring old age and not taking office.

units.zh: 各以壽終。
units.en: Both died in honored old age.
units.literal: Each ended life at a full old age.

units.zh: 譙秀，字元彥，巴西人也。
units.en: Qiao Xiu, courtesy name Yuanyan, came from Baxi.
units.literal: Qiao Xiu, styled Yuanyan, was a man of Baxi.

units.zh: 祖周，以儒學著稱，顯明蜀朝。
units.en: His ancestor Qiao Zhou was a famed scholar of Shu Han.
units.literal: His ancestor Zhou was famed for Confucian learning and illustrious in the Shu court.

units.zh: 秀少而靜默，不交於世，知天下將亂，預絕人事，雖內外宗親，不與相見。
units.en: He foresaw chaos, cut ties, and would not even see kin.
units.literal: Xiu from youth was still and silent, did not associate with the world; knowing the realm would soon fall into chaos, beforehand cut off human affairs—even inner and outer lineage kin he did not meet.

units.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不就。
units.en: He refused every provincial summons.
units.literal: The commandery examined him filial and incorrupt; the province raised him cultivated talent; he took neither.

units.zh: 及李雄據蜀，略有巴西，雄叔父驤、驤子壽皆慕秀名，具束帛安車徵之，皆不應。
units.en: Li Xiong's clan offered carriage and silk; he ignored them all.
units.literal: When Li Xiong held Shu and occupied Baxi, Xiong's uncle Xiang and Xiang's son Shou both admired Xiu's name, fully preparing bundled silks and a sedan carriage to summon him; he answered neither.

units.zh: 常冠皮弁，弊衣，躬耕山藪。
units.en: He farmed in buckskin cap and rags.
units.literal: He constantly wore leather cap and tattered clothes, personally plowing mountain marsh.

units.zh: 龔壯常嘆服焉。
units.en: Gong Zhuang marveled at his resolve.
units.literal: Gong Zhuang often sighed in admiration at him.

units.zh: 桓溫滅蜀，上疏薦之，朝廷以秀年在篤老，兼道遠，故不徵，遣使敕所在四時存問。
units.en: Huan Wen recommended him after the conquest of Shu; the court, citing age and distance, only sent seasonal greetings.
units.literal: When Huan Wen destroyed Shu he submitted a memorial recommending him; the court, because Xiu's years were very old and moreover the road was distant, therefore did not summon him, but sent an envoy ordering the place to inquire seasonally.

units.zh: 尋而范賁、蕭敬相繼作亂，秀避難宕渠，鄉里宗族依憑之者以百數。
units.en: Soon Fan Ben and Xiao Jing rebelled in succession; Xiu fled to Dangqu, where hundreds of clansmen relied on him.
units.literal: Soon Fan Ben and Xiao Jing in succession rebelled; Xiu fled trouble to Dangqu; lineage and clan who relied on him numbered in the hundreds.

units.zh: 秀年出八十，眾人欲代之負擔，秀曰：「各有老弱，當先營護。
units.en: Past eighty, kin wished to carry his gear; he said, 'You have elders and babes to tend first.
units.literal: Xiu's years passed eighty; the crowd wished to carry his load for him; Xiu said, "Each has old and weak—one ought first to plan and protect them.

units.zh: 吾氣力猶足自堪，豈以垂朽之年累諸君也！」
units.en: I can still shoulder my pack—do not load my age on you.'
units.literal: My breath and strength still suffice to bear myself—how could I, in these withered years, burden you gentlemen!"

units.zh: 年九十餘卒。
units.en: He died past ninety.
units.literal: He died past ninety.

units.zh: 翟湯，字道深，尋陽人。
units.en: Zhai Tang, courtesy name Daoshen, was from Xunyang.
units.literal: Zhai Tang, styled Daoshen, was a man of Xunyang.

units.zh: 篤行純素，仁讓廉潔，不屑世事，耕而後食，人有饋贈，雖釜庾一無所受。
units.en: He was kind, frugal, refused gifts—even a pot of grain.
units.literal: He practiced earnestly, pure and plain, benevolent, yielding, honest, and clean; he disdained worldly affairs, plowed and afterward ate; if people sent gifts, even cauldrons and measures he accepted none of them.

units.zh: 永嘉末，寇害相繼，聞湯名德，皆不敢犯，鄉人賴之。
units.en: In Yongjia's chaos bandits spared his village for his name.
units.literal: At the end of Yongjia, bandit harm followed one after another; hearing Tang's name and virtue, none dared violate him; his townsfolk relied on him.

units.zh: 司徒王導辟，不就，隱于縣界南山。
units.en: Wang Dao summoned him; he hid on South Mountain.
units.literal: Minister Wang Dao summoned him; he did not go, and hid on South Mountain within the county border.

units.zh: 始安太守干寶與湯通家，遣船餉之，敕吏云：「翟公廉讓，卿致書訖，便委船還。」
units.en: Gan Bao, his kinsman-by-marriage, sent a boat of supplies, instructing the clerk, "Lord Zhai is honest and yielding—you, sir, when you have delivered the letter, then leave the boat and return."
units.literal: Prefect of Shi'an Gan Bao was connected by family to Tang and sent a boat to supply him, instructing the clerk, saying, "Lord Zhai is honest and yielding—you, sir, when you have delivered the letter, then leave the boat and return."

units.zh: 湯無人反致，乃貨易絹物，因寄還寶。
units.en: Zhai sold goods for silk and repaid him.
units.literal: Tang had no man to send it back; therefore he sold goods for silk and sent it back to Bao through a broker.

units.zh: 寶本以為惠，而更煩之，益愧歎焉。
units.en: Gan Bao meant a favor yet felt only shame and deeper respect.
units.literal: Bao had thought it a kindness, yet it only troubled him the more; he increased in shame and admiration.

units.zh: 咸康中，征西大將軍庾亮上疏薦之，成帝徵為國子博士，湯不起。
units.en: Yu Liang recommended him; Emperor Cheng named him national erudite; he stayed home.
units.literal: In Xiankang, General Who Stabilizes the West Yu Liang submitted a memorial recommending him; Emperor Cheng summoned him as national university erudite; Tang did not rise.

units.zh: 建元初，安西將軍庾翼北征石季龍，大發僮客以充戎役，敕有司特蠲湯所調。
units.en: Yu Yi's levy on retainers skipped Zhai Tang by edict.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, General Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi on northern campaign against Shi Hu greatly conscripted retainers and guests to fill military service, ordering the offices specially to remit Tang's levy.

units.zh: 湯悉推僕使委之鄉吏，吏奉旨一無所受，湯依所調限，放免其僕，使令編戶為百姓。
units.en: Zhai handed his servants to the clerk, refused special favor, and freed them to commoner status.
units.literal: Tang pushed all servants and handed them to the village clerk; the clerk, receiving the order, accepted nothing; Tang according to the conscription limit dismissed his servants, letting them register as common households.

units.zh: 康帝復以散騎常侍徵湯，固辭老疾，不至。
units.en: Emperor Kang summoned him as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; again he pleaded age.
units.literal: Emperor Kang again summoned Tang as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; he firmly declined on grounds of age and illness and did not arrive.

units.zh: 年七十三，卒於家。
units.en: He died at seventy-three at home.
units.literal: At seventy-three he died at home.

units.zh: 子莊，字祖休。
units.en: His son Zhai Zhuang, courtesy name Zuxiu.
units.literal: His son Zhuang, styled Zuxiu.

units.zh: 少以孝友著名，遵湯之操，不交人物，耕而後食，語不及俗，惟以弋釣為事。
units.en: Zhuang copied his father's life: farmed, fished, shunned gossip.
units.literal: In youth he was famed for filial piety and friendship; he observed Tang's conduct, did not associate with people, plowed and afterward ate, speech not touching the vulgar, only taking archery and fishing as occupation.

units.zh: 及長，不復獵。
units.en: As an adult he gave up hunting.
units.literal: When grown, he no longer hunted.

units.zh: 或問：「漁獵同是害生之事，而先生止去其一，何哉？」
units.en: Someone asked, "Fishing and hunting are alike in harming living things—yet the master only removes one; why?"
units.literal: Someone asked, "Fishing and hunting are alike in harming living things—yet the master only removes one; why?"

units.zh: 莊曰：「獵自我，釣自物，未能頓盡，故先節其甚者。
units.en: Zhuang said, 'Hunting is my cruelty; fish choose the hook—I curbed the worse first.
units.literal: Zhuang said, "Hunting comes from myself; fishing comes from the thing—I could not cut off both at once, therefore I first restrained the greater.

units.zh: 且夫貪餌吞鉤，豈我哉！」
units.en: Fish greedily take hooks—how is that my sin?'
units.literal: Moreover greed for bait and swallowing the hook—is that I!"

units.zh: 時人以為知言。
units.en: Listeners called it wise.
units.literal: People of the time considered it a knowing saying.

units.zh: 晚節亦不復釣，端居篳門，歠菽飲水。
units.en: Late in life he quit fishing too, lived on beans and water.
units.literal: In his late years he also no longer fished, sitting upright at a brushwood gate, sipping beans and drinking water.

units.zh: 州府禮命，及公車徵，並不就。
units.en: He refused every summons.
units.literal: Commandery and prefecture ritual summons and state carriage summons together he did not accept.

units.zh: 年五十六，卒。
units.en: He died at fifty-six.
units.literal: At fifty-six he died.

units.zh: 子矯，亦有高操，屢辭辟命。
units.en: His son Zhai Jiao kept the same path.
units.literal: His son Jiao also had lofty conduct, repeatedly declining summons.

units.zh: 矯子法賜，孝武帝以散騎郎徵，亦不至。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu summoned Fasi; he too stayed away.
units.literal: Jiao's son Fasi was summoned as attendant cavalier by Emperor Xiaowu and likewise did not arrive.

units.zh: 世有隱行云。
units.en: The family was called a line of recluses.
units.literal: The age said they had a lineage of hidden conduct.

units.zh: 郭翻，字長翔，武昌人也。
units.en: Guo Fan, courtesy name Changxiang, came from Wuchang.
units.literal: Guo Fan, styled Changxiang, was a man of Wuchang.

units.zh: 伯父訥，廣州刺史。
units.en: His uncle Guo Ne governed Guangzhou.
units.literal: His uncle by seniority Ne was governor of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 父察，安城太守。
units.en: His father Guo Cha governed Ancheng.
units.literal: His father Cha was governor of Ancheng.

units.zh: 翻少有志操，辭州郡辟及賢良之舉。
units.en: Youthful, he refused every nomination.
units.literal: Fan in youth had determination and conduct; he declined provincial summons and recommendations as worthy and good.

units.zh: 家於臨川，不交世事，惟以漁釣射獵為娛。
units.en: He lived in Linchuan on fishing and hunting.
units.literal: His household was at Linchuan; he did not touch worldly affairs, taking only fishing, angling, and hunting as pleasure.

units.zh: 居貧無業，欲墾荒田，先立表題，經年無主，然後乃作。
units.en: He marked abandoned land, waited a year, then plowed.
units.literal: Poor without livelihood, he wished to open wasteland; first he set up a marker inscription; after a full year without owner, then he worked it.

units.zh: 稻將熟，有認之者，悉推與之。
units.en: When a neighbor claimed the field, he gave the whole crop away.
units.literal: When the rice was about to ripen, someone claimed it; he entirely pushed it to him.

units.zh: 縣令聞而詰之，以稻還翻，翻遂不受。
units.en: The magistrate forced the rice back; Fan still refused.
units.literal: The magistrate heard and questioned him, returning the rice to Fan; Fan then would not accept.

units.zh: 嘗以車獵，去家百餘里，道中逢病人，以車送之，徒步而歸。
units.en: He gave his cart to a sick stranger and walked home.
units.literal: Once by cart he hunted, more than a hundred li from home; on the road he met a sick man, gave him the cart to send him, and walked back on foot.

units.zh: 其漁獵所得，或從買者，便與之而不取直，亦不告姓名。
units.en: He gave game to buyers, took no pay, left no name.
units.literal: What he gained by fishing and hunting, if there were buyers, he then gave it to them and did not take payment, nor did he tell his name.

units.zh: 由是士庶咸敬貴焉。
units.en: Gentry and commoners alike honored him.
units.literal: Thereby gentlemen and commoners alike revered him.

units.zh: 與翟湯俱為庾亮所薦，公車博士徵，不就。
units.en: Yu Liang recommended him with Zhai Tang; he ignored the summons as Erudite.
units.literal: Together with Zhai Tang he was recommended by Yu Liang; summoned erudite by state carriage; he did not go.

units.zh: 咸康末，乘小船暫歸武昌省墳墓，安西將軍庾翼以帝舅之重，躬往造翻，欲強起之。
units.en: Yu Yi, the emperor's uncle, boarded his skiff at Wuchang to drag him to office.
units.literal: At the end of Xiankang he rode a small boat briefly returning to Wuchang to visit tombs; General Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi, by weight of being the emperor's maternal uncle, in person went to visit Fan, wishing to force him to rise.

units.zh: 翻曰：「人性各有所短，焉可強逼！」
units.en: Fan said, 'Every man has limits—do not force mine.'
units.literal: Fan said, "Human nature each has its short—how can it be forced!"

units.zh: 翼又以其船小狹，欲引就大船。
units.en: Yi asked him onto a larger barge.
units.literal: Yi again because his boat was small and narrow wished to draw him to a great boat.

units.zh: 翻曰：「使君不以鄙賤而辱臨之，此固野人之舟也。」
units.en: Fan answered, 'This skiff suits a countryman; honor it as you find it.'
units.literal: Fan said, "If the commissioner does not disdain my base and lowly self and condescends to visit, this is indeed a wild man's boat."

units.zh: 翼俯屈入其船中，終日而去。
units.en: Yu Yi crawled into the tiny boat and sat with him all day.
units.literal: Yi bent low and entered his boat; all day then departed.

units.zh: 嘗墜刀于水，路人有為取者，因與之。
units.en: He dropped a knife in a stream; a farmer fished it out and Fan offered it as gift.
units.literal: Once he dropped a knife in the water; a passerby retrieved it for him, and he gave it to him.

units.zh: 路人不取，固辭，翻曰：「爾向不取，我豈能得！」
units.en: The man would not keep it; Fan said, 'If you had not retrieved it, how could I have gotten it?'
units.literal: The passerby would not take it and firmly declined; Fan said, "If you just now had not taken it, how could I have obtained it!"

units.zh: 路人曰：「我若取此，將為天地鬼神所責矣。」
units.en: The man said, 'If I kept it, heaven would blame me.'
units.literal: The passerby said, "If I took this, I would be blamed by heaven, earth, and the ghosts."

units.zh: 翻知其終不受，復沈刀于水。
units.en: Fan sank the knife again.
units.literal: Fan knew he in the end would not accept, again sank the knife in the water.

units.zh: 路人悵焉，乃復沈沒取之。
units.en: The farmer dove and brought it back, vexed.
units.literal: The passerby was disappointed; then again dived and retrieved it.

units.zh: 翻於是不逆其意，乃以十倍刀價與之。
units.en: Fan respected his wishes and paid him tenfold the knife's worth.
units.literal: Fan then did not go against his intent, then gave him ten times the knife's price.

units.zh: 其廉不受惠，皆此類也。
units.en: Such was his stubborn honesty.
units.literal: His honesty in not accepting favor was all of this sort.

units.zh: 卒於家。
units.en: He died at home.
units.literal: He died at home.

units.zh: 辛謐，字叔重，隴西狄道人也。
units.en: Xin Mi, courtesy name Shuzhong, came from Didao in Longxi.
units.literal: Xin Mi, styled Shuzhong, was a man of Didao in Longxi.

units.zh: 父怡，幽州刺史，世稱冠族。
units.en: His father Xin Yi governed Youzhou; the clan wore high caps in reputation.
units.literal: His father Yi was governor of Youzhou; the age called them a cap clan.

units.zh: 謐少有志尚，博學善屬文，工草隸書，為時楷法。
units.en: He was a scholar and calligrapher others copied.
units.literal: Mi in youth had aspiration and esteem, was broadly learned and skilled at composing texts, worked cursive and clerical script, and was model for the age.

units.zh: 性恬靜，不妄交遊。
units.en: He lived quietly and made few friends.
units.literal: By nature quiet and still, he did not rashly associate or roam.

units.zh: 召拜太子舍人、諸王文學，累徵不起。
units.en: The court named him tutor to princes; he never went.
units.literal: He was summoned and appointed heir-apparent attendant and literary instructor to the various princes; repeatedly summoned, he did not rise.

units.zh: 永嘉末，以謐兼散騎常侍，慰撫關中。
units.en: Late in Yongjia the court sent him west as envoy.
units.literal: At the end of Yongjia he was appointed concurrently attendant censor regular to comfort Guanzhong.

units.zh: 謐以洛陽將敗，故應之。
units.en: He went because he saw Luoyang falling.
units.literal: Mi because Luoyang was about to be defeated, therefore answered.

units.zh: 及長安陷沒于劉聰，聰拜太中大夫，固辭不受。
units.en: Liu Cong offered a grandee title; he refused.
units.literal: When Chang'an fell to Liu Cong, Cong appointed grand palace grandee; he firmly declined and would not accept.

units.zh: 又曆石勒、季龍之世，並不應辟命。
units.en: Shi Le and Shi Hu could not move him either.
units.literal: Again through the eras of Shi Le and Shi Hu he answered no summons.

units.zh: 雖處喪亂之中，頹然高邁，視榮利蔑如也。
units.en: Through war after war he stayed aloof from rank.
units.literal: Although he dwelt amid ruin and chaos, he was lofty and transcendent, looking on glory and profit as nothing.

units.zh: 及冉閔僭號，復備禮徵為太常，謐遺閔書曰：「昔許由辭堯，以天下讓之，全其清高之節。
units.en: When Ran Min seized the throne and offered the Grand Master of Ceremonies post, Xin wrote to Min, saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.
units.literal: When Ran Min usurped the title, again with full ritual he summoned him as grand master of ceremonies; Mi sent Min a letter saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.

units.zh: 伯夷去國，子推逃賞，皆顯史牒，傳之無窮。
units.en: Boyi and Jie Zitui fled power—names that never die.
units.literal: Boyi left the state; Zituo fled reward—all appear in the histories and transmit without end.

units.zh: 此往而不反者也。
units.en: They left court never to return.
units.literal: These went and did not return.

units.zh: 然賢人君子雖居廟堂之上，無異于山林之中，斯窮理盡性之妙，豈有識之者邪！
units.en: Yet a sage at court may be no different from a sage on the hill—who sees that truth?
units.literal: Yet worthy men and gentlemen, although they dwell atop the temple hall, are no different from being in mountains and forests—such is the subtlety of exhausting pattern and completing nature—how could there be those who recognize it!

units.zh: 是故不嬰於禍難者，非為避之，但冥心至趣而與吉會耳。
units.en: Those who escape calamity are not hiding—they simply still the heart until fortune finds them.
units.literal: Therefore those not entangled in disaster and harm are not thereby avoiding them; only silent mind and utmost purpose meet with auspiciousness.

units.zh: 謐聞物極則變，冬夏是也；
units.en: Xin Mi wrote that all things turn at the limit—winter and summer prove it.
units.literal: Mi heard that when a thing reaches its limit it changes—winter and summer are so;

units.zh: 致高則危，累棋是也。
units.en: Stack too high and you topple—like a tower of stones.
units.literal: to reach height is to be in danger—a piled chess tower is so.

units.zh: 君王功以成矣，而久處之，非所以顧萬全遠危亡之禍也。
units.en: Your merit is won; to cling to power is not the way to stay safe.
units.literal: The lord king's merit is already accomplished; yet to dwell long in it is not the way to look to complete safety and distance the calamity of ruin and death.

units.zh: 宜因茲大捷，歸身本朝，必有許由、伯夷之廉，享松喬之壽，永為世輔，豈不美哉！」
units.en: It is fitting to take this great victory to return your person to the proper court—surely you will have the honesty of Xu You and Boyi, enjoy the years of Chisong and Wang Qiao, forever be the age's pillar—how could it not be beautiful!"
units.literal: It is fitting to take this great victory to return your person to the proper court—surely you will have the honesty of Xu You and Boyi, enjoy the years of Chisong and Wang Qiao, forever be the age's pillar—how could it not be beautiful!"

units.zh: 因不食而卒。
units.en: He stopped eating and died.
units.literal: Thereupon he refused food and died.

units.zh: 劉驎之
units.en: Liu Linzhi
units.literal: Liu Linzhi

units.zh: 劉驎之，字子驥，南陽人，光祿大夫耽之族也。
units.en: Liu Linzhi, courtesy name Ziji, of Nanyang, was kin to Liu Dan.
units.literal: Liu Linzhi, styled Ziji, was a man of Nanyang, of the clan of grand master of the palace Liu Dan.

units.zh: 驎之少尚質素，虛退寡欲，不修儀操，人莫之知。
units.en: He loved plain living and shunned display—no one noticed him.
units.literal: Linzhi in youth esteemed plain simplicity, was empty and retiring with few desires, did not cultivate deportment or bearing—no one knew him.

units.zh: 好遊山澤，志存遁逸。
units.en: He wandered peaks and meant to hide.
units.literal: He loved to roam mountains and marshes; his intent lodged in flight and reclusion.

units.zh: 嘗采藥至衡山，深入忘反，見有一澗水，水南有二石囷，一囷閉，一囷開，水深廣不得過。
units.en: On Hengshan he found twin stone silos by a ford too deep to cross.
units.literal: Once gathering herbs he reached Mount Heng, went deep and forgot to return; he saw a stream; south of the water were two stone granaries, one closed, one open; the water was deep and wide and he could not cross.

units.zh: 欲還，失道，遇伐弓人，問徑，僅得還家。
units.en: He lost the trail until a woodcutter pointed the way home.
units.literal: Wishing to return, he lost the way; met a bow-cutter, asked the path, barely got home.

units.zh: 或說囷中皆仙靈方藥諸雜物，驎之欲更尋索，終不復知處也。
units.en: Some said the silos held immortal drugs; he searched again and never found them.
units.literal: Some said the granaries held immortal recipes and medicines and various things; Linzhi wished to search again, but never again knew the place.

units.zh: 車騎將軍桓沖聞其名，請為長史，驎之固辭不受。
units.en: Huan Chong offered chief clerk; he refused.
units.literal: General Who Chariots and Horses Huan Chong heard his name and invited him as chief clerk; Linzhi firmly declined and would not accept.

units.zh: 沖嘗到其家，驎之于樹條桑，使者致命，驎之曰：「使君既枉駕光臨，宜先詣家君。」
units.en: When Huan Chong called, Liu was in the mulberry tree and said, 'Honor my father first.'
units.literal: Chong once arrived at his house; Linzhi was picking mulberry on a branch; the envoy delivered the command; Linzhi said, "Since the commissioner has condescended to visit in person, he ought first to visit my father."

units.zh: 沖聞大愧，於是乃造其父。
units.en: Chong flushed and went in to greet the old man first.
units.literal: Chong heard and was greatly ashamed; thereupon he went to visit his father.

units.zh: 父命驎之，然後方還，拂短褐與沖言話。
units.en: His father sent him down; Liu brushed his coat and spoke with Chong.
units.literal: The father ordered Linzhi; only then did he return, brushing his short hemp coat and conversing with Chong.

units.zh: 父使驎之於內自持濁酒蔬菜供賓，沖敕人代驎之斟酌，父辭曰：「若使從者，非野人之意也。」
units.en: Liu served wine himself; when Chong sent a servant the father said, 'A rustic host pours his own cup.'
units.literal: The father had Linzhi inside personally hold turbid wine and vegetables to supply the guest; Chong ordered someone pour for Linzhi in his stead; the father declined, saying, "If you use followers, it is not the intent of a wild man."

units.zh: 沖慨然，至昏乃退。
units.en: Chong stayed until dusk, moved.
units.literal: Chong sighed; only at dusk did he withdraw.

units.zh: 驎之雖冠冕之族，信儀著於群小，凡廝伍之家婚娶葬送，無不躬自造焉。
units.en: Though born noble, he attended every poor neighbor's wedding and funeral.
units.literal: Although Linzhi was of a capped-and-ribbon clan, his trust and bearing showed among the petty folk; for weddings, burials, and send-offs of common hireling households, none did he not personally visit.

units.zh: 居於陽岐，在官道之側，人物來往，莫不投之。
units.en: His house stood by the post road; every traveler stopped for his charity.
units.literal: He dwelt at Yangqi, beside the official road; people and goods coming and going all turned in to him.

units.zh: 驎之躬自供給，士君子頗以勞累，更憚過焉。
units.en: He fed them all himself until travelers dreaded the detour.
units.literal: Linzhi personally supplied them; gentlemen thought it laborious and increasingly feared passing there.

units.zh: 凡人致贈，一無所受。
units.en: He took no gifts.
units.literal: Whatever people brought as gifts, he accepted none.

units.zh: 去驎之家百餘里，有一孤姥，病將死，歎息謂人曰：「誰當埋我，惟有劉長史耳！
units.en: A dying crone miles away cried, 'Only Liu will bury me!
units.literal: More than a hundred li from Linzhi's home was a lone old woman, ill and about to die, who sighed and said to people, "Who will bury me—only Chief Clerk Liu!

units.zh: 何由令知。」
units.en: How can he hear?'
units.literal: By what means can I let him know."

units.zh: 驎之先聞其有患，故往侯之，值其命終，乃身為營棺殯送之。
units.en: He had heard her cough, arrived as she died, and buried her himself.
units.literal: Linzhi had earlier heard she was ill, therefore went to inquire; it happened she expired at that moment; then he personally for her arranged coffin and burial and sent her off.

units.zh: 其仁愛隱惻若此。
units.en: Such was his kindness.
units.literal: His benevolence and hidden pity were like this.

units.zh: 卒以壽終。
units.en: He died in honored age.
units.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.

units.zh: 索襲，字偉祖，敦煌人也。
units.en: Suo Xi, courtesy name Weizu, came from Dunhuang.
units.literal: Suo Xi, styled Weizu, was a man of Dunhuang.

units.zh: 虛靖好學，不應州郡之命，舉孝廉、賢良方正，皆以疾辭。
units.en: He declined every nomination as ill.
units.literal: Empty and still, loving learning, he answered no commandery summons; recommended filial and incorrupt, worthy and upright—each time he declined on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 游思於陰陽之術，著天文地理十餘篇，多所啟發。
units.en: He wrote on heaven and earth and the dark arts.
units.literal: He roamed thought in yin-yang arts and composed more than ten pieces on astronomy and geography, much enlightening.

units.zh: 不與當世交通，或獨語獨笑，或長歎涕泣，或請問不言。
units.en: He muttered alone, wept alone, fell silent when questioned.
units.literal: He did not traffic with the age; sometimes he spoke alone and laughed alone, or long sighed and wept, or when asked questions would not speak.

units.zh: 張茂時，敦煌太守陰澹奇而造焉，經日忘反，出而歎曰：「索先生碩德名儒，真可以諮大義。」
units.en: Prefect Yin Dan spent a day with him and sighed, "Master Suo is a great virtue and famed Confucian—truly one may consult him on great right."
units.literal: Under Zhang Mao, Dunhuang prefect Yin Dan, marveling, visited him; for a full day he forgot to return, and coming out sighed, "Master Suo is a great virtue and famed Confucian—truly one may consult him on great right."

units.zh: 澹欲行鄉射之禮，請襲為三老，曰：「今四表輯寧，將行鄉射之禮，先生年耆望重，道冠一時，養老之義，實系儒賢。
units.en: Yin asked him to preside as village elder, saying, "Now within the four borders there is peace; we are about to perform the village archery rite; the master, old in years and heavy in repute, his Way caps the age—the meaning of supporting the aged truly hangs on such Confucian worthies.
units.literal: Dan wished to perform the village archery rite and invited Xi as elder of three, saying, "Now within the four borders there is peace; we are about to perform the village archery rite; the master, old in years and heavy in repute, his Way caps the age—the meaning of supporting the aged truly hangs on such Confucian worthies.

units.zh: 既樹非梧桐，而希鸞鳳降翼；
units.en: You are no phoenix tree yet hope phoenixes to roost—
units.literal: Yet though you have not planted a phoenix tree, you hope for phoenix wings to descend;

units.zh: 器謝曹公，而冀蓋公枉駕，誠非所謂也。
units.en: you are no Duke Cao yet hope sages to call—this will not do.
units.literal: though your vessel is not Lord Cao, you hope Master Gai will condescend to visit—indeed this is not what is called fitting.

units.zh: 然夫子至聖，有召赴焉；
units.en: Confucius answered summons—
units.literal: Yet the Master was utmost sage and when summoned went;

units.zh: 孟軻大德，無聘不至，蓋欲弘闡大猷，敷明道化故也。
units.en: Mencius waited for the right invite—both taught the world.
units.literal: Mencius had great virtue—without summons he did not arrive—because he wished to spread the great plan and make clear the transformation of the Way.

units.zh: 今之相屈，遵道崇教，非有爵位，意者或可然乎！」
units.en: I call you only to honor learning, not for rank—perhaps it may be so!"
units.literal: Now summoning you bends to the Way and honors teaching; there are no ranks and offices—perhaps it may be so!"

units.zh: 會病卒，時年七十九。
units.en: He died at seventy-nine.
units.literal: It happened he died of illness at age seventy-nine.

units.zh: 澹素服會葬，贈賤二萬。
units.en: Yin Dan mourned in undyed linen and sent twenty thousand cash.
units.literal: Dan in plain garb attended the funeral and presented two myriad cash of condolence.

units.zh: 澹曰：「世人之所有餘者，富貴也；
units.en: Yin said, 'The world hoards riches—
units.literal: Dan said, "What the world has in surplus is wealth and honor;

units.zh: 目之所好者，五色也；
units.en: eyes crave color—
units.literal: what the eye loves is the five colors;

units.zh: 耳之所玩者，五音也。
units.en: ears crave music.
units.literal: what the ear plays with is the five tones.

units.zh: 而先生棄眾人之所收，收眾人之所棄，味無味於慌惚之際，兼重玄於眾妙之內。
units.en: Master Suo chose poverty, tasted the void, doubled the mystery others flee.
units.literal: Yet the master casts aside what the multitude gathers, gathers what the multitude casts aside; he savors the tasteless in the vast blur, doubles dark mystery within the myriad subtleties.

units.zh: 宅不彌畝而志忽九州，形居塵俗而棲心天外，雖黔婁之高遠，莊生之不願，蔑以過也。」
units.en: His hut was tiny yet his mind held the empire; not even Zhuangzi outdid him.'
units.literal: His house does not fill a mu yet his intent forgets the nine provinces; his form dwells in dust and vulgarity yet his mind roosts beyond heaven—though Qian Lou's loftiness, Zhuangzi's unwillingness, none surpass this."

units.zh: 乃諡曰玄居先生。
units.en: They styled him Master of the Dark Retreat.
units.literal: Thereupon they gave the posthumous title Master of Mysterious Dwelling.

units.zh: 楊軻，天水人也。
units.en: Yang Ke of Tianshui.
units.literal: Yang Ke was a man of Tianshui.

units.zh: 少好《易》，長而不娶，學業精微，養徒數百，常食粗飲水，衣褐縕袍，人不堪其憂，而軻悠然自得，疏賓異客，音旨未曾交也。
units.en: He taught the Book of Changes, never married, lived on gruel, and refused small talk with strangers.
units.literal: In youth he loved the Changes; grown, he did not marry; his learning was minute and subtle; he fed several hundred disciples, constantly eating coarse food and drinking plain water, wearing hemp and padded robes; others could not endure his hardship, yet Ke was leisurely self-content; with distant guests and strange visitors he never exchanged words.

units.zh: 雖受業門徒，非入室弟子，莫昨親言。
units.en: Only handpicked disciples heard his voice in person.
units.literal: Although disciples received instruction, unless they were chamber disciples he did not personally speak.

units.zh: 欲所論授，須旁無雜人，授入室弟子，令遞相宣授。
units.en: He taught in secret, relayed through chosen disciples.
units.literal: What he wished to lecture he required that beside him be no miscellaneous people; he instructed chamber disciples and ordered them to pass it in relay.

units.zh: 劉曜僭號，徵拜太常，軻固辭不起，曜亦敬而不逼，遂隱於隴山。
units.en: Liu Yao named him Grand Master of Ceremonies; he withdrew to Longshan.
units.literal: When Liu Yao usurped the title, he summoned and appointed grand master of ceremonies; Ke firmly declined and would not rise; Yao also respected him and did not force him; then he hid on Long Mountain.

units.zh: 曜後為石勒所擒，秦人東徙，軻留長安。
units.en: When Liu Yao fell to Shi Le, Ke stayed in Chang'an.
units.literal: Later Yao was captured by Shi Le; Qin people moved east; Ke remained in Chang'an.

units.zh: 及石季龍嗣偽位。
units.en: Shi Hu took the throne—
units.literal: When Shi Hu succeeded to the false throne,

units.zh: 備玄纁束帛安車徵之，軻以疾辭。
units.en: Shi Hu sent silks and carriage; Ke pleaded sick.
units.literal: with dark and crimson silks and peace carriage he summoned him; Ke declined on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 迫之，乃發。
units.en: Forced, he went.
units.literal: Pressed, he then set out.

units.zh: 既見季龍，不拜，與語，不言，命舍之於永昌乙第。
units.en: He faced Shi Hu silent and upright, and was lodged in Yongchang.
units.literal: When he had seen Shi Hu, he did not bow; speaking with him, he did not speak; Hu ordered him lodged in the second house of Yongchang.

units.zh: 其有司以軻倨傲，請從大不敬論，季龍不從，下書任軻所尚。
units.en: Ministers wanted him executed for lese-majesty; Shi Hu refused and let him be.
units.literal: His officials, because Ke was arrogant, asked to apply the great irreverence statute; Hu did not follow, issued a document letting Ke follow what he esteemed.

units.zh: 軻在永昌，季龍每有饋餼，輒口授弟子，使為表謝，其文甚美，覽者歎有深致。
units.en: His thank-you letters through disciples were praised as profound.
units.literal: Ke in Yongchang—whenever Hu had gifts of food, he orally instructed disciples to compose memorials of thanks; the texts were very fine; readers sighed that they had deep meaning.

units.zh: 季龍欲觀其真趣，乃密令美女夜以動之，軻蕭然不顧。
units.en: Shi Hu sent a girl to tempt him; he never looked.
units.literal: Hu wished to observe his true temper; therefore secretly ordered a beauty at night to move him; Ke was bleakly unmoved.

units.zh: 又使人將其弟子盡行，遣魁壯羯士衣甲持刀，臨之以兵，並竊其所賜衣服而去，軻視而不信，了無懼色。
units.en: Soldiers stole his gifts and leveled swords; he showed no fear.
units.literal: Again he had people take away all his disciples, sent stalwart Jie soldiers in armor holding blades, threatened him with weapons, and together stole the clothes Hu had granted and departed; Ke looked but did not believe, utterly without fear.

units.zh: 常臥土床，覆以布被，倮寢其中，下無茵褥。
units.en: He slept naked on bare earth under a rag quilt.
units.literal: He constantly lay on an earthen bed covered with a cloth quilt, slept naked inside, below without mat or cushion.

units.zh: 潁川荀鋪，好奇之士也，造而談經，軻瞑目不答。
units.en: The eccentric Xun Pu debated him; Ke feigned sleep.
units.literal: Xun Pu of Yingchuan, a man who loved the strange, visited and discussed the classics; Ke closed his eyes and did not answer.

units.zh: 鋪發軻被露其形，大笑之。
units.en: Xun stripped his quilt and laughed.
units.literal: Pu lifted Ke's quilt and exposed his body, greatly laughing at him.

units.zh: 軻神體頹然，無驚怒之狀。
units.en: Ke never flinched.
units.literal: Ke's spirit and body were slack, without startled anger.

units.zh: 于時咸以為焦先之徒，未有能量其深淺也。
units.en: People compared him to Jiao Xian—none plumbed his depth.
units.literal: At the time all considered him of the class of Jiao Xian; none could measure his depth.

units.zh: 後上疏陳鄉思，求還，季龍送以安車蒲輪，蠲十戶供之。
units.en: He begged leave westward; Shi Hu sent carriage and ten tax-free households.
units.literal: Later he submitted a memorial stating homesickness, begging to return; Hu sent him with peace carriage and rush-wrapped wheels and remitted ten households to supply him.

units.zh: 自歸秦州，仍教授不絕。
units.en: Back home he kept teaching.
units.literal: Returning to Qinzhou, he still taught without cease.

units.zh: 其後秦人西奔涼州，軻弟子以牛負之，為戍軍追擒，並為所害。
units.en: Fleeing west, his ox-cart was overtaken by guards who killed master and pupils.
units.literal: Afterward when Qin people fled west to Liangzhou, Ke's disciples used an ox to carry him; border guards pursued and captured them, and together they were killed.

units.zh: 公孫鳳
units.en: Gongsun Feng
units.literal: Gongsun Feng

units.zh: 公孫鳳，字子鸞，上谷人也。
units.en: Gongsun Feng, courtesy name Ziluan, came from Shanggu.
units.literal: Gongsun Feng, styled Ziluan, was a man of Shanggu.

units.zh: 隱于昌黎之九城山谷，冬衣單布，寢處土床，夏則幷食於器，停令臭敗，然後食之。
units.en: He wintered in one layer, summered on rotted gruel in a jar.
units.literal: He hid in Jiucheng valley of Changli; in winter he wore single cloth, slept on a clay bed; in summer he put food together in a vessel, stopped it until it stank and rotted, then ate it.

units.zh: 彈琴吟詠，陶然自得，人咸異之，莫能測也。
units.en: He sang to his lute, self-content; none understood him.
units.literal: He plucked the zither and chanted, pottery pleased with himself; people all marveled and could not fathom him.

units.zh: 慕容暐以安車徵至鄴，及見暐，不言不拜，衣食舉動如在九城。
units.en: Murong Wei brought him to Ye; he still would not bow or speak.
units.literal: Murong Wei with peace carriage summoned him to Ye; when he saw Wei, he did not speak or bow; eating, clothing, and motions were as in Jiucheng.

units.zh: 賓客造請，鮮得與言。
units.en: Visitors seldom won a word.
units.literal: Guests who visited and requested rarely got to speak with him.

units.zh: 數年病卒。
units.en: He died after a few years.
units.literal: After several years he died of illness.

units.zh: 公孫永
units.en: Gongsun Yong
units.literal: Gongsun Yong

units.zh: 公孫永，字子陽，襄平人也。
units.en: Gongsun Yong, courtesy name Ziyang, came from Xiangping.
units.literal: Gongsun Yong, styled Ziyang, was a man of Xiangping.

units.zh: 少而好學恬虛，隱于平郭南山，不娶妻妾，非身所墾植，則不衣食之，吟詠岩間，欣然自得，年餘九十，操尚不虧。
units.en: He lived ninety years in the hills, eating only what he tilled.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning and quiet emptiness; he hid on South Mountain of Pingguo, did not take wife or concubine; what he had not personally opened and planted he did not eat or wear; chanting among the cliffs, pleased with himself, past ninety years his conduct did not fail.

units.zh: 與公孫鳳俱被容暐徵至鄴，及見暐，不拜，王公以下造之，皆不與言，雖經隆冬盛暑，端然自若。
units.en: He and Feng reached court; he bowed to no prince, spoke to no lord, winter or summer.
units.literal: Together with Gongsun Feng he was summoned by Murong Wei with tolerance to Ye; when he saw Wei, he did not bow; from princes and dukes downward who visited him, he spoke with none; though through deep winter and sweltering summer, he sat upright naturally.

units.zh: 一歲餘，詐狂，暐送之平郭。
units.en: After a year he played madman and Murong Wei sent him home.
units.literal: After more than a year he feigned madness; Wei sent him back to Pingguo.

units.zh: 後苻堅又將備禮徵之，難其年耆路遠，乃遣使者致問。
units.en: Fu Jian meant to summon him but sent only greetings because of age and distance.
units.literal: Later Fu Jian again wished with full ritual to summon him; troubled by his old age and the road's distance, he then sent an envoy to convey inquiry.

units.zh: 未至而永亡，堅深悼之，諡曰崇虛先生。
units.en: He died before Fu Jian's envoy came; Fu Jian mourned him as Master of Honored Void.
units.literal: Before the envoy arrived Yong died; Jian deeply mourned him and gave the posthumous title Master Who Honors Emptiness.

units.zh: 張忠，字巨和，中山人也。
units.en: Zhang Zhong, courtesy name Juhe, came from Zhongshan.
units.literal: Zhang Zhong, styled Juhe, was a man of Zhongshan.

units.zh: 永嘉之亂，隱于泰山。
units.en: When Yongjia fell he fled to Mount Tai.
units.literal: In the Yongjia disorders he hid on Mount Tai.

units.zh: 恬靜寡欲，清虛服氣，餐芝餌石，修導養之法。
units.en: He lived on qi, herbs, and elixirs.
units.literal: Quiet and still with few desires, clear and empty, he swallowed breath, ate mushroom and stone, practiced methods of guidance and nurturing.

units.zh: 冬則縕袍，夏則帶索，端拱若屍。
units.en: Winter coat, summer rope—he sat like a corpse.
units.literal: In winter he wore padded robe; in summer girdle-rope; sitting upright like a corpse.

units.zh: 無琴書之適，不修經典，勸教但以至道虛無為宗。
units.en: He taught the wordless Way, not the canon.
units.literal: He had no zither or books for pleasure, did not polish the classics; in instruction he took only utmost Way and emptiness as ancestor.

units.zh: 其居依崇岩幽谷，鑿地為窟室。
units.en: He carved a cave in the cliff.
units.literal: His dwelling leaned on lofty crags and hidden valleys; he dug earth for a pit-chamber.

units.zh: 弟子亦以窟居，去忠六十餘步，五日一朝。
units.en: Pupils lived in nearby caves and visited every five days.
units.literal: Disciples also dwelt in pits, sixty-some paces from Zhong, paying court once every five days.

units.zh: 其教以形不以言，弟子受業，觀形而退。
units.en: He taught by gesture, not lecture.
units.literal: His teaching used form, not speech; disciples received the teaching, observed the form, and withdrew.

units.zh: 立道壇於窟上，每旦朝拜之。
units.en: Each dawn he bowed to a stone altar.
units.literal: He set a Way altar atop the pit; each dawn he bowed toward it.

units.zh: 食用瓦器，鑿石為釜。
units.en: He ate from pottery, cooked in stone pots.
units.literal: For food he used pottery vessels and carved stone for a cauldron.

units.zh: 左右居人饋之衣食，一無所受。
units.en: Neighbors offered clothes; he refused.
units.literal: Neighbors left him food and clothing; he accepted none.

units.zh: 好事少年頗或問以水旱之祥，忠曰：「天不言而四時行焉，萬物生焉，陰陽之事非窮山野叟所能知之。」
units.en: Asked about omens he said, 'Heaven needs no words to run the seasons—what would I know of yin and yang?'
units.literal: Curious youths sometimes asked about omens of flood or drought; Zhong said, "Heaven does not speak yet the four seasons proceed; the myriad things are born; matters of yin and yang are not what a poor old man of the deep mountains can know."

units.zh: 其遣諸外物，皆此類也。
units.en: He brushed the world off so in every case.
units.literal: His pushing away the various outer things was all of this sort.

units.zh: 年在期頤，而視聽無爽。
units.en: Past a hundred he saw and heard clearly.
units.literal: His years reached the hundred-cycle yet sight and hearing were unimpaired.

units.zh: 苻堅遣使徵之。
units.en: Fu Jian summoned him.
units.literal: Fu Jian sent an envoy to summon him.

units.zh: 使者至，忠沐浴而起，謂弟子曰：「吾餘年無幾，不可以逆時主之意。」
units.en: He bathed and told his pupils, 'I am old—I cannot defy an emperor's call.'
units.literal: When the envoy arrived, Zhong bathed and rose, saying to disciples, "My remaining years are not many; I may not oppose the intent of the ruler of the age."

units.zh: 浴訖就車。
units.en: He mounted the carriage when dry.
units.literal: When the bath finished he boarded the cart.

units.zh: 及至長安，堅賜以冠衣，辭曰：「年朽發落，不堪衣冠，請以野服入覲。」
units.en: In Chang'an he refused court dress: 'Let this wild man meet you in hemp.'
units.literal: Arriving at Chang'an, Jian granted him cap and robes; he declined, saying, "Years rotted, hair fallen—I cannot bear cap and robes; please let me enter audience in wild dress."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Fu Jian agreed.
units.literal: He followed it.

units.zh: 及見，堅謂之曰：「先生考磐山林，研精道素，獨善之美有餘，兼濟之功未也。
units.en: Fu Jian said, 'You perfected the private Way—now help the world.
units.literal: When they met, Jian said to him, "Sir, you have examined the rock in mountains and forests, ground fine the Way in plainness; the beauty of cultivating alone is more than enough, yet the work of aiding all is not yet done.

units.zh: 故遠屈先生，將任齊尚父。」
units.en: He offered him the role of Jiang Ziya to the king of Qi.'
units.literal: Therefore I have summoned you from afar, intending to appoint you like the Grand Duke of Qi to Shang."

units.zh: 忠曰：「昔因喪亂，避地泰山，與鳥獸為侶，以全朝夕之命。
units.en: Zhang Zhong answered, "I fled to Tai with the beasts to save my skin.
units.literal: Zhong said, "Formerly because of ruin and chaos I fled to Mount Tai, kept company with birds and beasts, to preserve life from dawn to dusk.

units.zh: 屬堯舜之世，思一奉聖顏。
units.en: I longed to see a sage king once.
units.literal: Now in a Yao-Shun age I wished once to behold the sage countenance.

units.zh: 年衰志謝，不堪展效，尚父之況，非敢竊擬。
units.en: I am too old for office—do not call me Jiang Ziya.
units.literal: Years decline and intent fades; I cannot bear to display service; the comparison to the Grand Duke is not what I dare steal.

units.zh: 山棲之性，情存岩岫，乞還餘齒，歸死岱宗。」
units.en: Let me end my days on sacred Tai."
units.literal: The nature of mountain roosting—my feeling lodges in crags and peaks; I beg to return my remaining years to die on Dai's lord.

units.zh: 堅以安車送之。
units.en: Fu Jian sent him home in the honor coach.
units.literal: Jian sent him back with peace carriage.

units.zh: 行達華山。
units.en: He reached Mount Hua westward.
units.literal: He traveled and reached Mount Hua.

units.zh: 歎曰：「我東嶽道士，沒于西嶽，命也，奈何！」
units.en: He cried, "An eastern hermit of the eastern marchmount dies on the western peak—fate! What can be done!"
units.literal: He sighed, saying, "I am an eastern marchmount Daoist who will perish on the western marchmount—fate—what can be done!

units.zh: 行五十里，及關而死。
units.en: Fifty li on he died at the barrier.
units.literal: He went fifty li and died at the pass.

units.zh: 使者馳驛白之，堅遣黃門郎韋華持節策吊，祀乙太牢，褒賜命服，諡曰安道先生。
units.en: Fu Jian sent rites, grand sacrifice, posthumous name Master of the Peaceful Way.
units.literal: The envoy raced post-horses to report; Jian sent palace attendant Wei Hua with staff of authority to convey condolences, sacrificed with grand tai lao, praised and granted mandated robes, posthumous title Master Who Pacifies the Way.

units.zh: 石垣，字洪孫，自雲北海劇人。
units.en: Shi Yuan claimed origin from Ju in Beihai.
units.literal: Shi Yuan, styled Hongsun, called himself a man of Ju in Beihai.

units.zh: 居無定所，不娶妻妾，不營產業，食不求美，衣必粗弊。
units.en: He wandered, no wife, no land, coarse food, ragged coat.
