units.literal: He dwelt without fixed place, did not take wife or concubine, did not manage property, did not seek fine food in eating, in clothing insisted on coarse and tattered.

units.zh: 或有遺其衣服，受而施人。
units.en: He passed on any gift of clothes.
units.literal: If someone left him clothing, he accepted and gave it away to others.

units.zh: 人有喪葬，輒杖策吊之。
units.en: He walked any distance to mourn the dead.
units.literal: When people had burials, he then staff in hand went to condole.

units.zh: 路無遠近，時有寒暑，必在其中；
units.en: Heat or cold, near or far, he always arrived—
units.literal: Whether the road was far or near, sometimes in cold or heat, he was always among them;

units.zh: 或同日共時，咸皆見焉。
units.en: sometimes the same mourners saw him twice at once.
units.literal: or on the same day at the same time, all saw him.

units.zh: 又能暗中取物，如晝無差。
units.en: He could pick objects in pitch dark as if at noon.
units.literal: Moreover he could take objects in the dark as in daylight without error.

units.zh: 姚萇之亂，莫知所終。
units.en: He vanished in Yao Chang's rebellion.
units.literal: In Yao Chang's disorders none knew where he ended.

units.zh: 宋纖，字令艾，敦煌效穀人也。
units.en: Song Xian, courtesy name Ling'ai, from Xiaogu in Dunhuang.
units.literal: Song Xian, styled Ling'ai, was a man of Xiaogu in Dunhuang.

units.zh: 少有遠操，沈靖不與世交，隱居于酒泉南山。
units.en: He hid on Jiuquan South Mountain.
units.literal: In youth he had far-reaching conduct, sunk in stillness, not associating with the world; he hid on South Mountain of Jiuquan.

units.zh: 明究經緯，弟子受業三千餘人。
units.en: He thoroughly investigated the classics and weft texts; registered disciples numbered more than three thousand.
units.literal: He clearly investigated classics and weft texts; disciples who received instruction were more than three thousand.

units.zh: 不應州郡辟命，惟與陰顒、齊好友善。
units.en: He spoke only to Yin Yong and Qi Hao.
units.literal: He answered no provincial or commandery summons; only with Yin Yong and Qi Hao was he friendly.

units.zh: 張祚時，太守楊宣畫其象於閣上；
units.en: Prefect Yang Xuan hung his portrait in the gallery—
units.literal: Under Zhang Zuo, Prefect Yang Xuan painted his likeness in the pavilion;

units.zh: 出入視之，作頌曰：「為枕何石？
units.en: and wrote, 'What stone for pillow?
units.literal: going out and in he looked at it and composed a praise, saying, "For pillow what stone?

units.zh: 為瀨何流？
units.en: What rapid for ford?
units.literal: For rapid what stream?

units.zh: 身不可見，名不可求。」
units.en: The man stays hidden—only the name rings.'
units.literal: The body cannot be seen; the name cannot be sought."

units.zh: 酒泉太守馬岌，高尚之士也，具威儀，鳴鐃鼓，造焉。
units.en: Prefect Ma Ji marched with full pomp to call.
units.literal: Jiuquan Prefect Ma Ji, a man of lofty conduct, fully set out guards, beat gongs and drums, and visited him.

units.zh: 纖高樓重閣，距而不見。
units.en: Song Xian barred his high gate.
units.literal: Xian in a high tower and double gallery kept distance and would not see him.

units.zh: 岌歎曰：「名可聞而身不可見，德可仰而形不可睹，吾而今而後知先生人中之龍也。」
units.en: Ma Ji sighed, 'Hearing his name yet never his face—he is a dragon among men.'
units.literal: Ji sighed, saying, "The name can be heard yet the body cannot be seen; virtue can be looked up to yet form cannot be viewed—I from today onward know the master is a dragon among men."

units.zh: 銘詩於石壁曰：「丹崖百丈，青壁萬尋。
units.en: He carved on the cliff, saying, "Cinnabar cliff a hundred yards, green cliff ten thousand fathoms.
units.literal: He inscribed a poem on the stone cliff, saying, "Cinnabar cliff a hundred yards, green cliff ten thousand fathoms.

units.zh: 奇木蓊鬱，蔚若鄧林。
units.en: trees thick as the magic grove—
units.literal: Strange trees luxuriant, lush as Deng's grove.

units.zh: 其人如玉，維國之琛。
units.en: that man is jade, the state's jewel—
units.literal: That man is like jade, the state's precious gem.

units.zh: 室邇人遐，實勞我心。」
units.en: The chamber is near, the man far—truly it wearies my heart."
units.literal: The chamber is near, the man far—truly it wearies my heart."

units.zh: 纖注《論語》，及為詩頌數萬言。
units.en: He wrote ten thousand words of poetry and Analects notes.
units.literal: Xian annotated the Analects and moreover composed poems and praises numbering ten thousand words.

units.zh: 年八十，篤學不倦。
units.en: At eighty he still studied.
units.literal: At eighty he loved learning and did not tire.

units.zh: 張祚後遣使者張興備禮徵為太子友，興逼喻甚切，纖喟然歎曰：「德非莊生，才非幹木，何取稽停明命！」
units.en: Zhang Zuo summoned him as crown prince's friend; he sighed, 'I am no Zhuangzi—why defy a clear edict?'
units.literal: After Zhang Zuo later sent envoy Zhang Xing with full ritual to summon him as friend to the heir apparent, Xing pressed the instruction very urgently; Xian sighed and said, "Virtue I am not Zhuangzi; talent I am not Duanmu Gan—why take delay in stopping the bright command!"

units.zh: 遂隨興至姑臧。
units.en: He went to Guzang.
units.literal: Thereupon he followed Xing to Guzang.

units.zh: 祚遣其太子太和以執友禮造之，纖稱疾不見，贈遺一皆不受。
units.en: The crown prince called; he feigned illness and took no gifts.
units.literal: Zuo sent his heir apparent Taihe to visit him with the rite of equal friend; Xian claimed illness and would not see him, and accepted none of the gifts.

units.zh: 尋遷太子太傅。
units.en: Soon he was made grand tutor.
units.literal: Soon he was moved to grand tutor to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 頃之，上疏曰：「臣受生方外，心慕太古。
units.en: He memorialized, 'I was born for the hills, my heart in high antiquity.
units.literal: Before long he submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject received life outside the square, heart admiring high antiquity.

units.zh: 生不喜存，死不悲沒。
units.en: Life does not delight me; death will not grieve me.
units.literal: In life I do not rejoice in surviving; in death I do not grieve perishing.

units.zh: 素有遺屬，屬諸知識，在山投山，臨水投水，處澤露形，在人親土。
units.en: Bury me in mountain stone or river—no word home.
units.literal: Plainly I have left instructions to my friends: in mountains cast me in mountains, by water cast in water, in marshes expose the form, among men kin the earth.

units.zh: 聲聞書疏，勿告我家。
units.en: Let no letter reach my kin.
units.literal: If sound or letter comes, do not tell my household.

units.zh: 今當命終，乞如素願。」
units.en: Now I ask only that wish.'
units.literal: Now as I am about to end life, I beg according to my plain wish."

units.zh: 遂不食而卒，時年八十二，諡曰玄虛先生。
units.en: He fasted to death at eighty-two, styled Master of Dark Void.
units.literal: Thereupon he refused food and died at age eighty-two; posthumous title Master of Mysterious Emptiness.

units.zh: 郭荷，字承休，略陽人也。
units.en: Guo He, courtesy name Chengxiu, from Lueyang.
units.literal: Guo He, styled Chengxiu, was a man of Lueyang.

units.zh: 六世祖整，漢安順之世，公府八辟，公車五徵，皆不就。
units.en: Ancestor Guo Zheng refused eight ducal calls and five carriages under the Han.
units.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zheng, in the reigns of Emperors An and Shun of Han, was summoned eight times by the highest offices and five times by state carriage, but accepted none.

units.zh: 自整及荷，世以經學致位。
units.en: The clan rose on the classics for generations.
units.literal: From Zheng down to He, generation after generation rose by classical learning.

units.zh: 荷明究群籍，特善史書。
units.en: Guo He mastered every corpus, best in histories.
units.literal: He clearly investigated all writings, especially skilled in histories.

units.zh: 不應州郡之命。
units.en: He refused local office.
units.literal: He answered no commandery orders.

units.zh: 張祚遣使者以安車束帛徵為博士祭酒，使者迫而致之。
units.en: Zhang Zuo's envoy dragged him to the libationer post.
units.literal: Zhang Zuo sent envoys with peace carriage and bundled silks to summon him as libationer erudite; the envoy forced him and brought him.

units.zh: 及至，署太子友。
units.en: At court they named him the crown prince's companion.
units.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed friend to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 荷上疏乞還，祚許之，遣以安車蒲輪送還張掖東山。
units.en: He memorialized for release and rode home to eastern Zhangye.
units.literal: He submitted a memorial begging to return; Zuo permitted it, sending him with peace carriage and rush-wrapped wheels back to East Mountain in Zhangye.

units.zh: 年八十四卒，諡曰玄德先生。
units.en: He died at eighty-four as Master of Dark Power.
units.literal: At eighty-four he died; posthumous title Master of Mysterious Virtue.

units.zh: 郭瑀，字元瑜，敦煌人也。
units.en: Guo Yu, courtesy name Yuanyu, from Dunhuang.
units.literal: Guo Yu, styled Yuanyu, was a man of Dunhuang.

units.zh: 少有超俗之操，東遊張掖，師事郭荷，盡傳其業。
units.en: He studied under Guo He in Zhangye.
units.literal: In youth he had conduct surpassing the vulgar; he east wandered to Zhangye and studied under Guo He, fully receiving his enterprise.

units.zh: 精通經義，雅辯談論，多才藝，善屬文。
units.en: He debated well and wrote well.
units.literal: He penetrated the classics' meaning, was refined in debate, had many talents, skilled at composing texts.

units.zh: 荷卒，瑀以為父生之，師成之，君爵之，而五服之制，師不服重，蓋聖人謙也，遂服斬衰，廬墓三年。
units.en: He mourned his teacher Guo He with three years' sackcloth by the grave.
units.literal: When He died, Yu considered that the father begat him, the teacher completed him, the lord ennobled him, yet in the five garments' system the teacher does not wear heavy mourning—because the sages were modest—thereupon he wore hemmed sackcloth and hut by the tomb three years.

units.zh: 禮畢，隱於臨松薤穀，鑿石窟而居，服柏實以輕身，作《春秋墨說》、《孝經錯緯》，弟子著錄千餘人。
units.en: He carved a cave in Linsong, ate pine nuts, wrote commentaries, taught a thousand pupils.
units.literal: When rites were finished, he hid at Xie Valley of Linsong, chiseled a stone grotto and dwelt, ate cypress fruit to lighten the body, composed "Spring and Autumn Ink Discourse" and "Disordered Wefts of the Classic of Filial Piety"; registered disciples numbered over a thousand.

units.zh: 張天賜遣使者孟公明持節，以浦輪玄纁備禮徵之，遺瑀書曰：「先生潛光九皋，懷真獨遠，心與至境冥符，志與四時消息，豈知蒼生倒懸，四海待拯者乎！
units.en: Zhang Tianci wrote, "Sir, you hide your gleam in the nine marshes, embrace the true alone far off; heart silently matches the utmost realm, intent with the four seasons waxes and wanes—do you not know the black-haired people hang upside down, the four seas await rescue!
units.literal: Zhang Tianci sent envoy Meng Gongming with staff, with rush wheels and dark silks in full ritual to summon him, leaving Yu a letter saying, "Sir, you hide your gleam in the nine marshes, embrace the true alone far off; heart silently matches the utmost realm, intent with the four seasons waxes and wanes—do you not know the black-haired people hang upside down, the four seas await rescue!

units.zh: 孤忝承時運，負荷大業，思與賢明同贊帝道。
units.en: The prince asked him to join the government.
units.literal: I shamefully inherit the season's fortune, bear the great enterprise, wish with the wise and clear jointly assist the imperial Way.

units.zh: 昔傳說龍翔殷朝，尚父鷹揚周室，孔聖車不停軌，墨子駕不俟旦，皆以黔首之禍不可以不救，君不獨立，道由人弘故也。
units.en: He cited Fu Yue, Jiang Ziya, Confucius, Mozi.
units.literal: In old days Fu Yue soared in Yin court, the Grand Duke hawk-displayed in Zhou house, Confucius' cart did not stop its tracks, Mozi's carriage did not wait for dawn—all because the black-haired people's calamity could not go unaided, the lord does not stand alone, the Way is enlarged by men.

units.zh: 況今九服分為狄場，二都盡為戎穴，天子僻陋江東，名教淪于左衽，創毒之甚，開避未聞。
units.en: He said Jin was cornered east while the north fell to barbarians.
units.literal: Moreover now the nine domains are split into Di arenas; both capitals are wholly barbarian dens; the Son of Heaven is cramped in humble Jiang east; name-teaching sinks under left-lapel; the wound of creation—such opening and fleeing has not been heard.

units.zh: 先生懷濟世之才，坐觀而不救，其于仁智，孤竊惑焉。
units.en: He asked how a sage could watch and not save.
units.literal: Sir, you embrace talent to aid the age, yet sit and watch without saving—in regard to benevolence and wisdom, I alone am puzzled.

units.zh: 故遣使者虛左授綏，鶴企先生，乃眷下國。」
units.en: Therefore I send an envoy, emptying the left seat and handing the tether, crane-standing for the sir, turning fondly to the lower state."
units.literal: Therefore I send an envoy, emptying the left seat and handing the tether, crane-standing for the sir, turning fondly to the lower state."

units.zh: 公明至山，瑀指翔鴻以示之曰：「此鳥也，安可籠哉！」
units.en: Guo Yu pointed at wild geese: 'You cannot cage that bird.'
units.literal: When Gongming reached the mountain, Yu pointed to soaring wild geese and showed him, saying, "This is a bird—how can it be caged!"

units.zh: 遂深逃絕迹。
units.en: He fled deeper into the hills.
units.literal: Thereupon he fled deep and cut off traces.

units.zh: 公明拘其門人，瑀歎曰：「吾逃祿，非避罪也，豈得隱居行義，害及門人！」
units.en: When pupils were seized he said, 'I flee salary, not justice—I cannot let pupils suffer.'
units.literal: Gongming seized his disciples; Yu sighed, saying, "I fled stipend, not crime—how can I keep hidden conduct and righteousness yet harm disciples!"

units.zh: 乃出而就徵。
units.en: He went to court.
units.literal: Thereupon he came out and answered the summons.

units.zh: 及至姑臧，值天賜母卒，瑀括發入吊，三踴而出，還于南山。
units.en: He mourned Tianci's mother with curt rites then fled back south.
units.literal: Arriving at Guzang, it happened Tianci's mother died; Yu tied hair and entered to condole, leapt the three leaps and came out, returned to South Mountain.

units.zh: 及天錫滅，苻堅又以安車徵瑀定禮儀，會父喪而止，太守辛章遣書生三百人就受業焉。
units.en: Fu Jian later summoned him for rites; father's death stopped him; three hundred students came to his cliff.
units.literal: When Tianci fell, Fu Jian again with peace carriage summoned Yu to fix ritual; it happened his father died and stopped; Prefect Xin Zhang sent three hundred students to receive instruction.

units.zh: 及苻氏之末，略陽王穆起兵酒泉，以應張大豫，遣使招瑀。
units.en: Wang Mu rebelled in Jiuquan and called on Guo Yu.
units.literal: At the end of the Fu clan, Lueyang Wang Mu raised troops in Jiuquan to answer Zhang Dayu and sent an envoy to summon Yu.

units.zh: 瑀歎曰：「臨河救溺，不卜命之短長；
units.en: He said, 'To save a drowning man you do not cast lots—
units.literal: Yu sighed, saying, "To save the drowning by the river, one does not divine whether life is short or long;

units.zh: 脈病三年，不豫絕其餐饋；
units.en: to nurse a patient three years you do not withhold food—
units.literal: to nurse sickness three years, one does not beforehand cut off meals;

units.zh: 魯連在趙，義不結舌，況人將左衽而不救之！」
units.en: Lu Lian never held his tongue—how can I stay silent while men go barbarian?'
units.literal: Lu Lian, when in Zhao, would not in righteousness keep silent—how much less can I fail to save men when they are about to wear their lapels on the left!"

units.zh: 乃與敦煌索嘏起兵五千，運粟三萬石，東應王穆。
units.en: He raised five thousand men and thirty thousand shi for Wang Mu.
units.literal: Thereupon with Su Gu of Dunhuang he raised troops five thousand, transported grain thirty thousand shi, east to answer Wang Mu.

units.zh: 穆以瑀為太府左長史、軍師將軍。
units.en: Wang Mu made him chief clerk and strategist.
units.literal: Mu made Yu grand clerk of the treasury on the left and army director.

units.zh: 雖居元佐，而口詠黃老，冀功成世定，追伯成之蹤。
units.en: Though a minister he chanted Daoism, dreaming of returning like Bo Cheng.
units.literal: Although he occupied chief aide, his mouth chanted Huang-Lao, hoping when merit was done and the age settled to follow the tracks of Bo Cheng.

units.zh: 穆惑於讒間，西伐索嘏，瑀諫曰：「昔漢定天下，然後誅功臣。
units.en: He warned Wang Mu, saying, "In old days when Han settled the realm, afterward they executed the merit ministers.
units.literal: Mu was deluded by slander between factions, west attacked Su Gu; Yu remonstrated, saying, "In old days when Han settled the realm, afterward they executed the merit ministers.

units.zh: 今事業未建而誅之，立見麋鹿游於此庭矣。」
units.en: Now the enterprise is not yet established yet you execute them—standing soon you will see deer roam this court."
units.literal: Now the enterprise is not yet established yet you execute them—standing soon you will see deer roam this court.

units.zh: 穆不從。
units.en: Wang Mu ignored him.
units.literal: Mu would not follow.

units.zh: 瑀出城大哭，舉手謝城曰：「吾不復見汝矣！」
units.en: He wept at the gate, 'I will not see this city again.'
units.literal: Yu went out of the city and greatly wept, raised his hands and thanked the city, saying, "I shall not see you again!"

units.zh: 還而引被覆面，不與人言，不食七日，與疾而歸，旦夕祈死。
units.en: He hid under his quilt, fasted seven days, begged for death.
units.literal: Returning he pulled the quilt over his face, spoke with no one, did not eat seven days, feigned illness and returned, morning and evening prayed for death.

units.zh: 夜夢乘青龍上天，至屋而止，寤而歎曰：「龍飛在天，今止於屋。
units.en: He dreamed riding a green dragon up to heaven, stopping at the roof; waking he sighed, saying, "The dragon flies in heaven; now it stops at the roof.
units.literal: At night he dreamed riding a green dragon up to heaven, stopping at the roof; waking he sighed, saying, "The dragon flies in heaven; now it stops at the roof.

units.zh: 屋之為字，尸下至也。
units.en: 'Roof' writes as 'arrive' beneath 'corpse'—
units.literal: In the character for 'roof', 'arrive' stands beneath 'corpse';

units.zh: 龍飛至尸，吾其死也。
units.en: a dragon to a corpse means I die.
units.literal: the dragon flies to corpse—I am about to die.

units.zh: 古之君子不卒內寢，況吾正士乎！」
units.en: The gentlemen of old did not end inside the inner chamber—how much more I, an upright man!"
units.literal: The gentlemen of old did not end inside the inner chamber—how much more I, an upright man!"

units.zh: 遂還酒泉南山赤崖閣，飲氣而卒。
units.en: He returned to Chiya pavilion and died meditating.
units.literal: Thereupon he returned to Red Cliff Pavilion on South Mountain of Jiuquan and expired by breath-control.

units.zh: 祈嘉，字孔賓，酒泉人也。
units.en: Qi Jia, courtesy name Kongbin, from Jiuquan.
units.literal: Qi Jia, styled Kongbin, was a man of Jiuquan.

units.zh: 少清貧，好學。
units.en: He was poor and book-loving.
units.literal: In youth he was clear and poor, loving learning.

units.zh: 年二十餘，夜忽窗中有聲呼曰：「祈孔賓，祈孔賓！
units.en: At night a voice called, "Qi Kongbin, Qi Kongbin!
units.literal: Past twenty, at night suddenly in the window a voice called, "Qi Kongbin, Qi Kongbin!

units.zh: 隱去來，隱去來！
units.en: Flee and hide, flee and hide!
units.literal: Hide away, come hide away!

units.zh: 修飾人世，甚苦不可諧。
units.en: The world bruises those who dress it—
units.literal: To polish and trim the human world is very bitter and cannot be harmonized;

units.zh: 所得未毛銖，所喪如山崖。」
units.en: what you gain is not yet a hair's tip; what you lose is like a mountain cliff."
units.literal: what you gain is not yet a hair's tip; what you lose is like a mountain cliff."

units.zh: 旦而逃去，西至敦煌，依學官誦書，貧無衣食，為書生都養以自給，遂博通經傳，精究大義。
units.en: He fled to Dunhuang, worked as a school cook, and became a scholar.
units.literal: At dawn he fled away, west to Dunhuang, relied on the school officer to recite books; poor without clothes or food, he became steward for the students to supply himself; thereby he broadly penetrated the classics and traditions, finely investigated great meanings.

units.zh: 西游海渚，教授門生百餘人。
units.en: He taught a hundred pupils on the western shore.
units.literal: He west wandered to sea islets and taught more than a hundred disciples.

units.zh: 張重華徵為儒林祭酒。
units.en: Zhang Chonghua named him erudite libationer.
units.literal: Zhang Chonghua summoned him as libationer of the forest of scholars.

units.zh: 性和裕，教授不倦，依《孝經》作《二九神經》。
units.en: He wrote the Two-Nine Spirit Classic from the Filial Piety, teaching without weariness.
units.literal: By nature harmonious and ample, he taught tirelessly, relying on the Classic of Filial Piety to compose the "Two-Nine Spirit Classic".

units.zh: 在朝卿士、郡縣守令彭和正等受業獨拜床下者二千餘人，天錫謂為先生而不名之。
units.en: Two thousand officials bowed to Qi Jia as 'Master' without daring his name.
units.literal: At court ministers, commandery and county magistrates such as Peng Hezheng and others who received instruction, alone bowing at the couch-side, numbered more than two thousand; Tianci called him Master and did not use his name.

units.zh: 竟以壽終。
units.en: He died full of years.
units.literal: In the end he ended life at a full old age.

units.zh: 瞿硎先生
units.en: Master of the Quxing Cliff
units.literal: Master of the Quxing Cliff

units.zh: 瞿硎先生者，不得姓名，亦不知何許人也。
units.en: The recluse of Quxing cliff—name and home unknown.
units.literal: The Master of the Quxing cliff—his name could not be obtained, nor was it known what place he was from.

units.zh: 太和末，常居宣城郡界文脊山中，山有瞿硎，因以為名焉。
units.en: He lived on Mount Wenji in Xuancheng near the Quxing grotto.
units.literal: At the end of Taihe he constantly dwelt within the bounds of Xuancheng commandery on Mount Wenji; the mountain had a Quxing cliff, and by this he took his name.

units.zh: 大司馬桓溫嘗往造之。
units.en: Huan Wen climbed to his cave.
units.literal: Grand marshal Huan Wen once went to visit him.

units.zh: 既至，見先生被鹿裘，坐於石室，神無忤色，溫及僚佐數十人皆莫測之，乃命伏滔為之銘贊。
units.en: Huan found him in deerskin in a stone room, baffled his retinue, and had Fu Tao write his praise.
units.literal: When he arrived, he saw the master draped in deerskin, sitting in a stone chamber, spirit without offending color; Wen and several tens of aides and staff all could not fathom him; then he ordered Fu Tao to compose an inscription and praise for him.

units.zh: 竟卒於山中。
units.en: He died in the hills.
units.literal: In the end he died in the mountains.

units.zh: 謝敷，字慶緒，會稽人也。
units.en: Xie Fu, courtesy name Qingxu, from Kuaiji.
units.literal: Xie Fu, styled Qingxu, was a man of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 性澄靖寡欲，入太平山十餘年。
units.en: He hid on Mount Taiping ten years.
units.literal: By nature clear, still, with few desires, he entered Mount Taiping more than ten years.

units.zh: 鎮軍郗愔召為主簿，台徵博士，皆不就。
units.en: Xi Yin and the ministry summoned him; he refused.
units.literal: General Who Stabilizes the Army Xi Yin summoned him as chief clerk; the ministry summoned him as erudite—he took neither.

units.zh: 初，月犯少微，少微一名處士星，占者以陷士當之。
units.en: A moon omen touched the hermit star—seers said a recluse would die.
units.literal: At first, the moon trespassed on Shaowei; Shaowei has another name, the star of retired scholars; astrologers thought it meant a scholar would fall.

units.zh: 譙國戴逵有美才，人或憂之。
units.en: People feared for Dai Kui.
units.literal: Dai Kui of Qiao had fine talent; some worried for him.

units.zh: 俄而敷死，故會稽人士以嘲吳人云：「吳中高士，便是求死不得死。」
units.en: When Xie Fu died, Kuaiji wits mocked Wu: 'Their hermits cannot even manage to die.'
units.literal: Soon Fu died; therefore men of Kuaiji to mock men of Wu said, "Among Wu's lofty gentlemen, they are the sort who seek death yet cannot die."

units.zh: 戴逵，字安道，譙國人也。
units.en: Dai Kui, courtesy name Andao, from Qiao.
units.literal: Dai Kui, styled Andao, was a man of Qiao.

units.zh: 少博學，好談論，善屬文，能鼓琴，工書畫，其餘巧藝靡不畢綜。
units.en: He mastered debate, letters, lute, painting, and every art.
units.literal: In youth he was broadly learned, loved discussion, skilled at composing texts, could strum the zither, was skilled at calligraphy and painting; of the other clever arts none he did not combine.

units.zh: 總角時，以雞卵汁溲白瓦屑作《鄭玄碑》，又為文而自鐫之，詞麗器妙，時人莫不驚歎。
units.en: As a boy he carved a Zheng Xuan stele in mortar—crowds marveled.
units.literal: In boyhood he kneaded egg white with white tile crumbs to make a Zheng Xuan stele, also composed the text and personally engraved it; the words lovely, the vessel subtle—people of the time none did not marvel.

units.zh: 性不樂當世，常以琴書自娛。
units.en: He lived for lute and books, not office.
units.literal: By nature he did not delight in serving the age; constantly he took zither and books to amuse himself.

units.zh: 師事術士范宣于豫章，宣異之，以兄女妻焉。
units.en: His teacher Fan Xuan gave him a niece in marriage.
units.literal: He studied under the specialist Fan Xuan in Yuzhang; Xuan marveled at him and gave him his elder brother's daughter as wife.

units.zh: 太宰、武陵王晞聞其善鼓琴，使人召之，逵對使者破琴曰：「戴安道不為王門伶人！」
units.en: Prince Xi summoned him to play; Kui smashed his lute: 'I will not be a prince's jester.'
units.literal: The grand steward and prince of Wuling, Xi, hearing he was skilled at the zither, sent men to summon him; Kui to the envoy broke the zither, saying, "Dai Andao will not be a house entertainer to princes!"

units.zh: 晞怒，乃更引其兄述。
units.en: Xi called his brother Dai Shu instead.
units.literal: Xi was angry, then instead summoned his elder brother Shu.

units.zh: 述聞命欣然，擁琴而往。
units.en: Shu happily took his lute to the palace.
units.literal: Shu hearing the order was pleased, hugging his zither and going.

units.zh: 逵後徙居會稽之剡縣。
units.en: Kui moved to Shan in Kuaiji.
units.literal: Kui afterward moved to dwell in Shan county of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 性高潔，常以禮度自處，深以放達為非道，乃著論曰：
units.en: He condemned 'free and easy' excess and wrote:
units.literal: By nature lofty and clean, he constantly used ritual measure to order himself; deeply he took unrestrained license as not the Way; therefore he composed a treatise, saying:

units.zh: 夫親沒而采藥不反者，不仁之子也；
units.en: To roam while parents need you is unfilial;
units.literal: For parents to die yet one gathers herbs and does not return—such is an unfilial son;

units.zh: 君危而屢出近關者，苟免之臣也。
units.en: to bolt the border while the throne totters is cowardice.
units.literal: for the lord to be in peril yet one repeatedly goes out near the passes—such is a minister who seeks bare escape.

units.zh: 而古之人未始以彼害名教之體者何？
units.en: The ancients never let conduct wreck the teaching—why?
units.literal: Yet the men of old never began to let those things harm the substance of name-teaching—why?

units.zh: 達其旨故也。
units.en: They grasped the meaning.
units.literal: Because they grasped the meaning, therefore they did.

units.zh: 達其旨，故不惑其跡。
units.en: Knowing the root, they ignored the pose.
units.literal: Because they grasped the meaning, therefore they were not deluded by traces.

units.zh: 若元康之人，可謂好遁跡而不求其本，故有捐本徇末之弊，舍實逐聲之行，是猶美西施而學其顰眉，慕有道而折其巾角，所以為慕者，非其所以為美，徒貴貌似而已矣。
units.en: He mocked Yuankang poseurs who mimicked reclusion without virtue.
units.literal: As for the men of Yuankang, one may say they loved hiding traces but did not seek the root; therefore there was the fault of casting away the root and pursuing the twigs, conduct of abandoning substance and chasing rumor—it is like admiring Xishi and studying her knitted brow, admiring the Way yet folding the kerchief corners; what they admired was not what made beauty beautiful; they valued only seeming resemblance.

units.zh: 夫紫之亂硃，以其似硃也。
units.en: Purple passes for crimson because it looks like crimson.
units.literal: Purple confuses vermilion because it resembles vermilion.

units.zh: 故鄉原似中和，所以亂德；
units.en: Village worthies mimic the mean and rot virtue;
units.literal: Therefore the village worthy resembles the mean—thereby he confuses virtue;

units.zh: 放者似達，所以亂道。
units.en: libertines mimic freedom and ruin the Way.
units.literal: the unrestrained resemble free passage—thereby they confuse the Way.

units.zh: 然竹林之為放，有疾而為顰者也，元康之為放，無德而折巾者也，可無察乎！
units.en: Bamboo Grove had excuse; Yuankang only aped the scarf.
units.literal: Yet the Bamboo Grove's unrestraint was having illness and thereby knitting the brow; Yuankang's unrestraint was lacking virtue yet folding the kerchief—can one fail to examine!

units.zh: 且儒家尚譽者，本以興賢也，既失其本，則有色取之行。
units.en: Confucians chase fame and lose the substance.
units.literal: Moreover Confucians who esteem fame originally meant to raise the worthy; once they lose the root, then there is conduct of seizing color.

units.zh: 懷情喪真，以容貌相欺，其弊必至於末偽。
units.en: They trade masks until all truth dies.
units.literal: Harbor feeling and lose the genuine, cheat one another with looks—the fault must reach utmost falsity.

units.zh: 道家去名者，欲以篤實也，苟失其本，又有越檢之行。
units.en: Daoists flee names yet leap bounds.
units.literal: Daoists who cast away names wished to make solid truth; if they lose the root, again there is conduct that leaps the norm.

units.zh: 情禮俱虧，則仰詠兼忘，其弊必至於本薄。
units.en: Both schools thin to hypocrisy.
units.literal: When feeling and ritual both fail, then they look up chanting both forgotten—the fault must reach root thinness.

units.zh: 夫偽薄者，非二本之失，而為弊者必托二本以自通。
units.en: As for the falsely thin, that is not a failure of the two roots; rather, those who create the abuse must borrow the two roots to excuse themselves.
units.literal: The falsely thin are not the two roots' failure, but those who make the fault must borrow the two roots to excuse themselves.

units.zh: 夫道有常經而弊無常情，是以六經有失，王政有弊，苟乖其本，固聖賢所無奈何也。
units.en: When the root rots, neither sage can save it.
units.literal: The Way has constant classics but faults have no constant temper; therefore the six classics have failures, royal government has faults; if one strays from the root, indeed even sages and worthies cannot help it.

units.zh: 嗟夫！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 行道之人自非性足體備、暗蹈而當者，亦曷能不棲情古烈，擬規前修。
units.en: Unless you are born whole, model the ancients with care.
units.literal: Men who walk the Way, unless nature is complete in the body and they darkly tread what fits, how can they not lodge feeling in ancient ardor and model former cultivation.

units.zh: 苟迷擬之然後動，議之然後言，固當先辯其趣舍之極，求其用心之本，識其枉尺直尋之旨，采其被褐懷玉之由。
units.en: Judge ends and means before you act.
units.literal: If only after delusion in modeling one moves, after deliberation one speaks, one must first distinguish the utmost of choosing and rejecting, seek the root of the mind's use, know the meaning of bending a foot to gain a fathom, gather the reason for wearing coarse cloth while cherishing jade.

units.zh: 若斯，途雖殊，而其歸可觀也；
units.en: Paths differ yet aim one way;
units.literal: If so, though roads differ, their convergence can be observed;

units.zh: 跡雖亂，而其契不乖也。
units.en: tracks tangle yet the tally holds.
units.literal: though traces are tangled, their tally is not wrong.

units.zh: 不然，則流遁忘反，為風波之行，自驅以物，自誑以偽，外眩囂華，內喪道實，以矜尚奪其真主，以塵垢翳其天正，貽笑千載，可不慎歟！
units.en: Else you chase fashion, lose the core, and earn a thousand years' mockery.
units.literal: If not, then drifting one forgets the return, making conduct of wind and wave, driving oneself with things, deceiving oneself with sham, outwardly dazzled by clamorous splendor, inwardly losing the Way's substance, letting boastfulness rob the true lord, letting dust and filth dim heaven's uprightness—laughter for a thousand ages—can one not be cautious!

units.zh: 孝武帝時，以散騎常侍、國子博士累徵，辭父疾不就。
units.en: Xiaowu called him to court; he pleaded his father's health.
units.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was repeatedly summoned as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance and Erudite of the Academy of the Sons of the State; he declined on account of his father's illness and did not go.

units.zh: 郡縣敦逼不已，乃逃于吳。
units.en: Officials hounded him until he fled to Wu.
units.literal: Commandery and county pressed urgently; then he fled to Wu.

units.zh: 吳國內史王珣有別館在武丘山，逵潛詣之，與珣遊處積旬。
units.en: He hid with Wang Xun on Mount Wuqiu for weeks.
units.literal: Interior secretary of Wu Wang Xun had a separate lodge on Mount Wuqiu; Kui secretly went to him and with Xun roamed and dwelt accumulating ten days.

units.zh: 會稽內史謝玄慮逵遠遁不反，乃上疏曰：「伏見譙國戴逵希心俗表，不嬰世務，棲遲衡門，與琴書為友。
units.en: Xie Xuan memorialized, saying, "I humbly see Dai Kui of Qiao set his heart outside the vulgar, not entangle in worldly affairs, linger at a brushwood gate, befriend zither and books.
units.literal: Interior secretary of Kuaiji Xie Xuan, worrying Kui would flee far and not return, therefore submitted a memorial, saying, "I humbly see Dai Kui of Qiao set his heart outside the vulgar, not entangle in worldly affairs, linger at a brushwood gate, befriend zither and books.

units.zh: 雖策命屢加，幽操不回，超然絕跡，自求其志。
units.en: Summons never moved his resolve.
units.literal: Although summons with tally came many times, his hidden resolve did not turn; transcendentally he cut traces and sought his intent.

units.zh: 且年垂耳順，常抱羸疾，時或失適，轉至委篤。
units.en: He was past sixty and frail.
units.literal: Moreover years hung near ear-harmony; he constantly embraced a wasting illness; sometimes unwell, it turned to utter exhaustion.

units.zh: 今王命未回，將離風霜之患。
units.en: Another summons might kill him.
units.literal: Now the king's command has not returned; he will leave wind and frost's affliction.

units.zh: 陛下既已愛而器之，亦宜使其身名並存，請絕其召命。」
units.en: Your majesty already loves and treasures him—you ought also to let body and name together survive; I beg cut off his summons."
units.literal: Your majesty already loves and treasures him—you ought also to let body and name together survive; I beg cut off his summons."

units.zh: 疏奏，帝許之，逵復還剡。
units.en: The emperor agreed; Dai Kui went home to Shan.
units.literal: When the memorial was presented, the emperor permitted it; Kui again returned to Shan.

units.zh: 後王珣為尚書僕射，上疏復請徵為國子祭酒，加散騎常侍，徵之，復不至。
units.en: Wang Xun tried again; Dai stayed away.
units.literal: Later, when Wang Xun became Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, he submitted a memorial again requesting that Dai Kui be summoned as Libationer of the Academy of the Sons of the State, with the additional office of Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; Dai was summoned but again did not arrive.

units.zh: 太元二十年，皇太子始出東宮，太子太傳會稽王道子、少傅王雅、詹事王珣又上疏曰：「逵執操貞厲，含味獨遊，年在耆老，清風彌劭。
units.en: The eastern palace memorialized, saying, "Kui holds conduct chaste and stern, tastes meaning alone and roams; years in hoary age, pure wind ever stronger.
units.literal: In the twentieth year of Taiyuan, when the crown prince first left the eastern palace, grand tutor to the crown prince Dao Wang Daozi, junior tutor Wang Ya, and chamberlain Wang Xun again submitted a memorial, saying, "Kui holds conduct chaste and stern, tastes meaning alone and roams; years in hoary age, pure wind ever stronger.

units.zh: 東宮虛德，式延事外，宜加旌命，以參僚侍。
units.en: They wanted him as palace tutor.
units.literal: The eastern palace lacks virtue; the model extends beyond service; it is fitting to add bannered mandate to join the staff and attend.

units.zh: 逵既重幽居之操，必以難進為美，宜下所在備禮發遣。」
units.en: Kui since he esteems hidden dwelling's conduct, surely takes hard to advance as beautiful; it is fitting to order the place to prepare ritual and dispatch."
units.literal: Kui since he esteems hidden dwelling's conduct, surely takes hard to advance as beautiful; it is fitting to order the place to prepare ritual and dispatch."

units.zh: 會病卒。
units.en: He died before taking the post.
units.literal: It happened he died of illness.

units.zh: 長子勃，有父風。
units.en: His son Dai Bo matched his spirit.
units.literal: The eldest son Bo had the father's air.

units.zh: 義熙初，以散騎侍郎徵，不起，尋卒。
units.en: Dai Bo was summoned in Yixi and died unreached.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, summoned as attendant gentleman cavalier, he did not rise; soon he died.

units.zh: 龔玄之
units.en: Gong Xuanzhi
units.literal: Gong Xuanzhi

units.zh: 龔玄之，字道玄，武陵漢壽人也。
units.en: Gong Xuanzhi, courtesy name Daoxuan, from Hanshou in Wuling.
units.literal: Gong Xuanzhi, styled Daoxuan, was a man of Hanshou in Wuling.

units.zh: 父登，歷長沙相、散騎常侍。
units.en: His father Gong Deng had been minister and attendant.
units.literal: His father Deng had served as Minister of Changsha and Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance.

units.zh: 玄之好學潛默，安於陋巷。
units.en: He loved books and quiet alleys.
units.literal: Xuanzhi loved learning and was silent, content in a poor lane.

units.zh: 州舉秀才，公府辟，不就。
units.en: He refused nominations.
units.literal: The province raised him cultivated talent; the ducal offices summoned him; he did not go.

units.zh: 孝武帝下詔曰：「夫哲王禦世，必搜揚幽隱，故空谷流縶維之詠，丘園旅束帛之觀。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict, saying, "When a wise king governs the age, he must search and raise the hidden; therefore empty valleys flow the ode of the white horse, hill gardens display bundled silks.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict, saying, "When a wise king governs the age, he must search and raise the hidden; therefore empty valleys flow the ode of the white horse, hill gardens display bundled silks.

units.zh: 譙國戴逵、武陵龔玄之並高尚其操，依仁遊藝，潔己貞鮮，學弘儒業，朕虛懷久矣。
units.en: The edict paired Dai Kui and Gong Xuanzhi.
units.literal: Dai Kui of Qiao and Gong Xuanzhi of Wuling together are lofty in conduct, rely on benevolence and roam in arts, cleanse themselves chaste and fresh, learning broadens Confucian enterprise; I have long held an empty bosom toward them.

units.zh: 二三君子，豈其戢賢於懷抱哉！
units.en: Why hide such men?
units.literal: You several gentlemen—how could you hoard worthies in your bosom!

units.zh: 思挹雅言，虛誠諷議，可並以為散騎常侍，領國子博士，指下所在備禮發遣，不得循常，以稽側席之望。」
units.en: I wish to draw upon their refined words and sincerely seek their counsel. Both may be appointed Gentlemen-in-Regular-Attendance while concurrently serving as Erudites of the Academy of the Sons of the State; order the local authorities to prepare the rites and send them on without following routine and thereby delaying my expectant hope."
units.literal: I wish to draw upon their refined words and sincerely seek their counsel. Both may be appointed Gentlemen-in-Regular-Attendance while concurrently serving as Erudites of the Academy of the Sons of the State; order the local authorities to prepare the rites and send them on without following routine and thereby delaying my expectant hope."

units.zh: 郡縣敦逼，苦辭疾篤，不行。
units.en: County officers pressed; both pleaded mortal illness.
units.literal: Commandery and county pressed urgently; he bitterly pleaded grave illness; did not go.

units.zh: 尋卒，時年五十八。
units.en: Gong died at fifty-eight.
units.literal: Soon he died at age fifty-eight.

units.zh: 弟子元壽，亦有德操，高尚不仕，舉秀才及州辟召，並稱疾不就。
units.en: His pupil Yuan Shou also refused office.
units.literal: The disciple Yuan Shou also had virtue and conduct, lofty and not serving; raised cultivated talent and provincial summons together he claimed illness and did not go.

units.zh: 孝武帝以太學博士、散騎侍郎、給事中累徵，遂不起。
units.en: Xiaowu hounded Yuan Shou in vain.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu repeatedly summoned him as grand university erudite, attendant gentleman cavalier, and palace counselor; in the end he did not rise.

units.zh: 卒於家。
units.en: Yuan died at home.
units.literal: He died at home.

units.zh: 陶淡，字處靜，太尉侃之孫也。
units.en: Tao Dan, courtesy name Chujing, was Tao Kan's grandson.
units.literal: Tao Dan, styled Chujing, was a grandson of Grand Commandant Kan.

units.zh: 父夏，以無行被廢。
units.en: His father Tao Xia was disgraced.
units.literal: His father Xia was dismissed for misconduct.

units.zh: 淡幼孤，好導養之術，謂仙道可祈。
units.en: Orphaned, he chased immortality.
units.literal: Dan in youth was orphaned, loved methods of guidance and nurturing, said the immortal Way could be prayed for.

units.zh: 年十五六，便服食絕穀，不婚娶。
units.en: He stopped eating grain and never wed.
units.literal: At fifteen or sixteen he swallowed elixirs and cut grain, did not marry.

units.zh: 家累千金，僮客百數，淡終日端拱，曾不營問。
units.en: He ignored vast wealth and many servants.
units.literal: Household piled a thousand in gold, retainers and guests in the hundreds; Dan all day sat upright, never managing or asking.

units.zh: 頗好讀《易》善卜筮。
units.en: He read the Book of Changes and divined.
units.literal: Somewhat he loved to read the Changes and was skilled at divination.

units.zh: 于長沙臨湘山中結廬居之，養一白鹿以自偶。
units.en: He built a hut in Linxiang hills with a white deer.
units.literal: On Mount Linxiang of Changsha he built a hut and dwelt, raising a white deer for company.

units.zh: 親故有候之者，輒移渡澗水，莫得近之。
units.en: He moved visitors across a stream they could not ford.
units.literal: When kin and old friends came to visit, he always moved them across a gully stream; none could draw near.

units.zh: 州舉秀才，淡聞，遂轉逃羅縣埤山中，終身不返，莫知所終。
units.en: When summoned he fled to Pi mountain and vanished.
units.literal: The province raised him cultivated talent; Dan hearing it, then turned and fled to Mount Pi in Luo county, to the end of life did not return; none knows where he ended.

units.zh: 陶潛，字元亮，大司馬侃之曾孫也。
units.en: Tao Qian (Yuanming), courtesy name Yuanliang, great-grandson of Tao Kan.
units.literal: Tao Qian, styled Yuanliang, was a great-grandson of Grand Commandant Kan.

units.zh: 祖茂，武昌太守。
units.en: His grandfather Tao Mao governed Wuchang.
units.literal: His grandfather Mao was governor of Wuchang.

units.zh: 潛少懷高尚，博學善屬文，穎脫不羈，任真自得，為鄉鄰之所貴。
units.en: Youthful, proud, learned, the hamlet esteemed him.
units.literal: Qian in youth cherished lofty conduct, was broadly learned and skilled at composing texts, outstanding and unbridled, yielding to truth and self-content; the village honored him.

units.zh: 嘗著《五柳先生傳》以自況曰：「先生不知何許人，不詳姓字，宅邊有五柳樹，因以為號焉。
units.en: He composed the "Biography of Master Five Willows" to compare himself, saying, "The master did not know what place he was from; surname and personal name not detailed; beside his house were five willow trees, and by this he took his sobriquet.
units.literal: Once he composed the "Biography of Master Five Willows" to compare himself, saying, "The master did not know what place he was from; surname and personal name not detailed; beside his house were five willow trees, and by this he took his sobriquet.

units.zh: 閒靜少言，不慕榮利。
units.en: Quiet, terse, no taste for rank.
units.literal: Leisurely quiet, few words, not admiring glory and profit.

units.zh: 好讀書，不求甚解，每有會意，欣然忘食。
units.en: He read for joy, not pedantry, and forgot meals when moved.
units.literal: He loved reading books, did not seek to penetrate deeply; whenever he had a meeting of meaning, gladly forgot eating.

units.zh: 性嗜酒，而家貧不能恆得。
units.en: He loved wine but stayed poor.
units.literal: By nature he loved wine, but the household was poor and could not constantly obtain it.

units.zh: 親舊知其如此，或置酒招之，造飲必盡，期在必醉。
units.en: Friends poured for him; he drank to blackout.
units.literal: Kin and old friends knowing this, sometimes set out wine and summoned him; when he went to drink he always finished, expecting surely to get drunk.

units.zh: 既醉而退，曾不吝情。
units.en: He left drunk without fuss.
units.literal: When drunk he withdrew, never stinting feeling.

units.zh: 環堵蕭然，不蔽風日，短褐穿結，簞瓢屢空，晏如也。
units.en: His hut leaked; he wore patches; his ladle was empty—yet he smiled.
units.literal: His ring of walls was bleak, not sheltering wind and sun; short coat patched and tied, gourd and ladle often empty—yet he was tranquil.

units.zh: 常著文章自娛，頗示己志，忘懷得失，以此自終。」
units.en: He constantly composed texts to amuse himself, somewhat showing his intent, forgetting gain and loss, by this ending himself."
units.literal: He constantly composed texts to amuse himself, somewhat showing his intent, forgetting gain and loss, by this ending himself."

units.zh: 其自序如此，時人謂之實錄。
units.en: People called his self-sketch honest.
units.literal: His self-account was thus; people of the time called it truthful record.

units.zh: 以親老家貧，起為州祭酒，不堪吏職，少日自解歸。
units.en: He took a small post for his parents' rice, quit at once.
units.literal: Because parents were old and household poor, he rose as libationer for the province; he could not bear clerical duty; in few days himself resigned and returned.

units.zh: 州召主簿，不就，躬耕自資，遂抱羸疾。
units.en: He refused clerkship, farmed, and fell ill.
units.literal: The province summoned him chief clerk; he did not go, personally plowing to supply himself; then he embraced a wasting illness.

units.zh: 復為鎮軍、建威參軍，謂親朋曰：「聊欲弦歌，以為三徑之資可乎？」
units.en: He said to kin and friends, "I merely wish to strum and sing to supply funds for three paths—may I?"
units.literal: Again he became adviser to the army who stabilizes and the army who establishes might; he said to kin and friends, "I merely wish to strum and sing to supply funds for three paths—may I?"

units.zh: 執事者聞之，以為彭澤令。
units.en: The court named him magistrate of Pengze.
units.literal: Those in charge hearing it, made him magistrate of Pengze.

units.zh: 在縣，公田悉令種秫穀，曰：「令吾常醉於酒足矣。」
units.en: In the county he ordered all public fields planted in glutinous millet, saying, "Let me always be drunk on wine—that is enough."
units.literal: In the county he ordered all public fields planted in glutinous millet, saying, "Let me always be drunk on wine—that is enough."

units.zh: 妻子固請種粳。
units.en: His family begged for food grain.
units.literal: Wife and children firmly begged to plant non-glutinous.

units.zh: 乃使一頃五十畝種秫，五十畝種粳。
units.en: He split the fields half for wine, half for rice.
units.literal: Then he made one qing fifty mu glutinous, fifty mu non-glutinous.

units.zh: 素簡貴，不私事上官。
units.en: He scorned toadying to superiors.
units.literal: Plain and simple he esteemed, did not privately serve superiors.

units.zh: 郡遣督郵至縣，吏白應束帶見之，潛歎曰：「吾不能為五斗米折腰，拳拳事鄉里小人邪！」
units.en: Qian sighed, saying, "I cannot for five pecks of rice bend my waist, diligently serving petty men of the village!"
units.literal: The commandery sent a postal inspector to the county; clerks reported he should bind his sash to see him; Qian sighed, saying, "I cannot for five pecks of rice bend my waist, diligently serving petty men of the village!"

units.zh: 義熙二年，解印去縣，乃賦《歸去來》。
units.en: In Yixi 2 he quit and wrote 'Returning Home.'
units.literal: In the second year of Yixi he unsealed the seal and left the county, then composed "Returning Home".

units.zh: 其辭曰：
units.en: It begins:
units.literal: Its text said:

units.zh: 歸去來兮，田園將蕪胡不歸？
units.en: Home again! The fields run wild—why stay away?
units.literal: Away home! The fields and gardens will waste—why not return?

units.zh: 既自以心為形役，奚惆悵而獨悲？
units.en: I let flesh rule soul—why grieve alone?
units.literal: Since I let the heart be slave to the body, why mourn alone in sorrow?

units.zh: 悟已往之不諫，知來者之可追。
units.en: Past faults cannot be mended; the future may yet be caught.
units.literal: I see the past cannot be remonstrated, yet what comes may still be pursued.

units.zh: 實迷途其未遠，覺今是而昨非。
units.en: I strayed but a little; today I know right from wrong.
units.literal: Truly the lost road is not far; I know today is right and yesterday wrong.

units.zh: 舟遙遙以輕颺，風飄飄而吹衣，問征夫以前路，恨晨光之希微。
units.en: Boat and breeze bear me; I ask the way; dawn comes too slow.
units.literal: The boat drifts lightly on the wave; the wind flutters blowing the robe; I ask the traveler the road ahead, resent the morning light's faint gleam.

units.zh: 乃瞻衡宇，載欣載奔。
units.en: I see my eaves and run.
units.literal: Then I gaze at my lintel, now glad, now running.

units.zh: 僮僕來迎，稚子侯門。
units.en: Boys wait at the gate.
units.literal: Servants come to welcome; children wait at the gate.

units.zh: 三徑就荒，松菊猶存。
units.en: Weeds choke the paths—pines and mums still stand.
units.literal: Three paths verge on waste, yet pines and chrysanthemums remain.

units.zh: 攜幼入室，有酒盈樽。
units.en: Wine brims the cup with children by my side.
units.literal: Leading the young inside, wine fills the cup.

units.zh: 引壺觚以自酌，眄庭柯以怡顏，倚南窗以寄傲，審容膝之易安。
units.en: I pour my own cup, smile at the trees, lean on the southern sill—this little room is enough.
units.literal: I lift the kettle and goblet to pour for myself, glance at the courtyard trees to ease my face, lean on the south window to lodge my pride, know that a space that fits the knees is easy to be at peace.

units.zh: 園日涉而成趣，門雖設而常關；
units.en: I stroll the garden daily; the gate stays shut;
units.literal: Daily I walk the garden and it grows delightful; though a gate is set, it is often shut;

units.zh: 策扶老而流憩，時翹首而遐觀。
units.en: I lean on a cane, lift my eyes to the hills.
units.literal: I lean on my staff and wander to rest, sometimes raise my head and gaze far.

units.zh: 雲無心而出岫，鳥倦飛而知還；
units.en: Clouds drift from peaks without a plan; tired birds know the way home;
units.literal: Clouds leave the peaks without intent; birds weary of flying know to return;

units.zh: 景翳翳其將入，撫孤松而盤桓。
units.en: Sunset dims; I linger by a lone pine.
units.literal: the sunlight dims as it is about to enter; I stroke the lone pine and linger.

units.zh: 歸去來兮，請息交以絕遊，世與我而相遺，復駕言兮焉求！
units.en: I end visits—world and I have parted—why chase more words?
units.literal: Away home! I beg to cease mixing and cut off wandering; the age and I forsake each other—why drive forth words and seek again!

units.zh: 悅親戚之情話，樂琴書以消憂。
units.en: Kin and books and lute melt my care.
units.literal: I delight in kin's heartfelt talk, take joy in zither and books to melt sorrow.

units.zh: 農人告餘以春暮，將有事乎西疇。
units.en: Farmers say spring is late—west field calls.
units.literal: The farmer tells me spring is late; work will begin in the western field.

units.zh: 或命巾車，或棹孤舟，既窈窕以尋壑，亦崎嶇而經丘。
units.en: Cart or skiff—winding dales, rugged hills.
units.literal: Sometimes order the scarf carriage, sometimes paddle a lone boat; both winding deep to seek ravines, also rugged crossing knolls.

units.zh: 木欣欣以向榮，泉涓涓而始流，善萬物之得時，感吾生之行休。
units.en: Woods thrive, springs run—I envy things their hour, know my life ebbs.
units.literal: Trees flourish toward glory; springs trickle beginning to flow; I marvel that the myriad things catch their season, yet feel my life will soon rest.

units.zh: 已矣乎！
units.en: Enough!
units.literal: Enough!

units.zh: 寓形宇內復幾時，曷不委心任去留，胡為乎遑遑欲何之？
units.en: Why not trust the heart to stay or go—why scurry with nowhere bound?
units.literal: How long will this form lodge in the universe—why not give the heart to go or stay—why hurry, hurry, whither would you go?

units.zh: 富貴非吾願，帝鄉不可期。
units.en: Rank is not my wish; heaven's court is not for me.
units.literal: Wealth and honor are not my wish; the imperial city cannot be counted on.

units.zh: 懷良晨以孤往，或植杖而芸秄，登東皋以舒嘯，臨清流而賦詩；
units.en: Dawn walks, weeding, whistle on the eastern mound, poems by the stream—
units.literal: I cherish fine mornings to go alone, or plant my staff and weed the glutinous, climb the eastern height to loose a long whistle, face clear stream and compose a poem;

units.zh: 聊乘化而歸盡，樂夫天命復奚疑！
units.en: I ride change to the end and doubt heaven no more!
units.literal: for now I ride transformation to the end, joyfully trust heaven's command—what doubt remains!

units.zh: 頃之，徵著作郎，不就。
units.en: The court called him editor; he stayed away.
units.literal: Before long he was summoned as editorialist; he did not go.

units.zh: 既絕州郡覲謁，其鄉親張野及周旋人羊松齡、寵遵等或有酒要之，或要之共至酒坐，雖不識主人，亦欣然無忤，酣醉便反。
units.en: He drank with anyone who offered, even strangers, until blind drunk.
units.literal: Having cut off commandery visits, if his townsman Zhang Ye and those he moved among such as Yang Songling and Pang Zun sometimes had wine and invited him, or invited him together to a wine seat, though he did not know the host, still he was pleased without offense, and when dead drunk then returned.

units.zh: 未嘗有所造詣，所之唯至田舍及廬山遊觀而已。
units.en: He only visited farms and Lu Mountain.
units.literal: He never made purposeful visits; where he went was only to farmsteads and to roam and view Mount Lu.

units.zh: 刺史王弘以元熙中臨州，甚欽遲之，後自造焉。
units.en: Wang Hong came to govern and longed to meet him.
units.literal: Inspector Wang Hong in the Yuanxi years came to the province, greatly admired and waited for him, afterward personally visited him.

units.zh: 潛稱疾不見，既而語人云：「我性不狎世，因疾守閑，幸非潔志慕聲，豈敢以王公紆軫為榮邪！
units.en: Qian claimed illness and would not see; afterward said to people, "My nature does not cozy with the world; because of illness I guard quiet—luckily it is not a clean intent admiring fame—how dare I take a prince's bending axle as glory!
units.literal: Qian claimed illness and would not see; afterward said to people, "My nature does not cozy with the world; because of illness I guard quiet—luckily it is not a clean intent admiring fame—how dare I take a prince's bending axle as glory!

units.zh: 夫謬以不賢，此劉公幹所以招謗君子，其罪不細也。」
units.en: To be wrongly deemed unworthy—that is why Liu Gonggan drew slander from gentlemen; the fault is not small."
units.literal: To be wrongly deemed unworthy—that is why Liu Gonggan drew slander from gentlemen; the fault is not small."

units.zh: 弘每令人候之，密知當往廬山，乃遣其故人龐通之等齎酒，先於半道要之。
units.en: Wang Hong sent a friend with wine mid-road to Lu.
units.literal: Hong always ordered men to watch him; secretly knowing he would go to Mount Lu, then sent his old friend Pang Tongzhi and others carrying wine beforehand to waylay him halfway.

units.zh: 潛既遇酒，便引酌野亭，欣然忘進。
units.en: Tao stopped for wine and forgot the journey.
units.literal: When Qian met the wine, he then drew drink in a wild pavilion, gladly forgot to advance.

units.zh: 弘乃出與相見，遂歡宴窮日。
units.en: Wang Hong joined the feast.
units.literal: Hong then came out and met him; then they feasted merrily all day.

units.zh: 潛無履，弘顧左右為之造履。
units.en: Tao had no shoes; Wang ordered sandals made.
units.literal: Qian had no sandals; Hong looked to left and right to have sandals made for him.

units.zh: 左右請履度，潛便於坐申腳令度焉。
units.en: Tao stretched his bare feet to be measured.
units.literal: Attendants asked for foot measure; Qian at the seat stretched out his feet and let them measure.

units.zh: 弘要之還州，問其所乘，答云：「素有腳疾，向乘藍輿，亦足自反。」
units.en: He answered, "Plainly I have foot ailment; lately I ride a blue litter—still enough to return myself."
units.literal: Hong invited him back to the province, asked what he rode; he answered, "Plainly I have foot ailment; lately I ride a blue litter—still enough to return myself."

units.zh: 乃令一門生二兒共轝之至州，而言笑賞適，不覺其有羨于華軒也。
units.en: Students carried his chair; he chatted as if no shame.
units.literal: Then he ordered one student and two sons together to carry him to the province, yet talking and laughing at ease, not letting them feel he envied splendid carriages.

units.zh: 弘後欲見，輒于林澤間候之。
units.en: Wang met him only in the wilds.
units.literal: Hong afterward when wishing to see him, then waited for him among woods and marshes.

units.zh: 至於酒米乏絕，亦時相贍。
units.en: Wang sent grain when the larder ran dry.
units.literal: As for when wine and rice failed, sometimes he also supplied him.

units.zh: 其親朋好事，或載酒肴而往，潛亦無所辭焉。
units.en: Friends brought feasts; he never refused.
units.literal: When kin and friends who loved affairs sometimes carried wine and dishes and went, Qian also declined none.

units.zh: 每一醉，則大適融然。
units.en: Each drunk brought pure joy.
units.literal: Each time drunk, then he was greatly pleased and melting.

units.zh: 又不營生業，家務悉委之兒僕。
units.en: He left chores to servants.
units.literal: Again he did not manage livelihood; household tasks he entirely entrusted to sons and servants.

units.zh: 未嘗有喜慍之色，惟遇酒則飲，時或無酒，亦雅詠不輟。
units.en: He showed no temper except toward wine; sober, he still sang.
units.literal: Never did he show joy or anger; only when he met wine he drank; sometimes when there was no wine, still he chanted elegantly without stopping.

units.zh: 嘗言夏月虛閑，高臥北窗之下，清風颯至，自謂羲皇上人。
units.en: Summer nap by the north window—he called himself older than history.
units.literal: He once said in summer months idle and quiet, lying high below the north window, when clear wind arrived in rustling gusts, he called himself a man before the Emperor Xi.

units.zh: 性不解音，而畜素琴一張，弦徽不具，每朋酒之會，則撫而和之，曰：「但識琴中趣，何勞弦上聲！」
units.en: He kept an unstrung zither: 'Taste the music in the mind, not the ear.'
units.literal: By nature he did not understand music, yet he kept one plain zither without strings and studs; whenever friends gathered with wine, then he stroked it in harmony, saying, "Only know the zither's inner interest—why trouble the sounds on the strings!"

units.zh: 以宋元嘉中卒，時年六十三，所有文集並行於世。
units.en: He died under Song at sixty-three; his works survive.
units.literal: He died in the Yuanjia period of Song at age sixty-three; his collected writings all circulated in the world.

units.zh: 史臣曰：君子之行殊途，顯晦之謂也。
units.en: The historian says: office and reclusion are one man's two roads.
units.literal: The historian says: The gentleman's path has many roads—this is called showing or hiding.

units.zh: 出則允釐庶政，以道濟時；
units.en: In court he orders the state;
units.literal: Going out, then he harmonizes the myriad policies and aids the age with the Way;

units.zh: 處則振拔囂埃，以卑自牧。
units.en: at home he washes off dust and feeds the soul.
units.literal: dwelling, then he shakes off clamor and dust and keeps low to nurture the self.

units.zh: 詳求厥義，其來夐矣。
units.en: Both ways are ancient.
units.literal: Examining closely their meaning, its origin is remote.

units.zh: 公和之居窟室，裳唯編草，誡叔夜而凝神鑒；
units.en: Sun Deng in his cave, clothed only in woven grass—
units.literal: Gonghe's dwelling in a pit-chamber, garments only woven grass—warning Shuye yet concentrating spirit mirror;

units.zh: 威輦之處叢祠，衣無全帛，對子荊而陳貞則：並滅景而弗追，柳禽、尚平之流亞。
units.en: Dong Jing lived among clustered shrines in clothes without a whole piece of silk and set forth a rule of integrity to Sun Chu; together these men hid their light beyond pursuit, successors to Liuxia Hui and Shang Ziping.
units.literal: Weinian's place among clustered shrines, clothes without whole silk—facing Zijing he set forth chaste rule: together they dimmed their gleam and would not be pursued—next in rank to Liuqin and Shangping.

units.zh: 夏統遠邇稱其孝友，宗党高其諒直，歌《小海》之曲。
units.en: Xia Tong's filial name rang far; his kin prized his blunt truth; when he sang the 'Little Sea'—
units.literal: Xia Tong far and near praised his filial piety and friendship; lineage honored his honesty and straightness; singing the song of the Little Sea—

units.zh: 則伍胥猶存；
units.en: Wu Zixu seemed to walk again;
units.literal: then Wu Zixu still survives;

units.zh: 固貞石之心，則公閭尤愧，時幸洛濱之觀，信乎茲言。
units.en: and that flint heart of his shamed even Jia Chong—on the Luo embankment the crowd saw it was true.
units.literal: as for the steadfast stone heart, then even Gonglu would feel shame; when they chanced on the sight at Luo's shore, truly this saying holds.

units.zh: 宋纖幼懷遠操，清規映拔，楊宣頌其畫象，馬岌歎其人龍，玄虛之號，實期為美。
units.en: Song Xian earned the name Master of Dark Void.
units.literal: Song Xian in youth cherished far-reaching conduct, pure measure shining transcendent; Yang Xuan praised his painted image; Ma Ji sighed he was a dragon among men—the title Mysterious Emptiness truly matched the beauty.

units.zh: 餘之數子，或移病而去官，或著論而矯俗，或箕踞而對時人，或弋釣而棲衡泌，含和隱璞，乘道匿輝，不屈其志，激清風于來葉者矣。
units.en: Others fled office, wrote, fished, hid jade in sackcloth—each stiffened the breeze for later ages.
units.literal: As for the several men beyond, some moved illness to leave office, some composed treatises to correct custom, some squatted with knees spread facing men of the time, some shot fish and lodged at brushwood gates—holding harmony, hiding the unpolished gem, riding the Way, concealing radiance, not bending their intent, stirring clear wind for later leaves.

units.zh: 贊曰：厚秩招累，修名順欲。
units.en: The verse says: fat pay brings grief; fame chains desire.
units.literal: The eulogy says: Thick salary summons trouble; polished name follows desire.

units.zh: 確乎群士，超然絕俗。
units.en: Yet these men stood clear of both.
units.literal: Firm are these gentlemen, transcendent beyond the vulgar.

units.zh: 養粹岩阿，銷聲林曲。
units.en: They fed the spirit in cliffs and woods.
units.literal: They nurtured purity in cliff hollows, erased sound in forest bends.

units.zh: 激貪止競，永垂高躅。
units.en: They shamed the greedy and left high footprints.
units.literal: They stung greed and stopped rivalry, forever leaving lofty tracks.
